title: fix(motion): hold the crossing law on corner arcs one corner at a time
body:
## What changed

Main is red on `corner_arc_radius` ("Waterline: no corner turned on an arc"). PR #2273 sent the rounded walks of Waterline and Offset rings through `post_crossing_free`. That law maps a crossing arc onto the vertices of the pass. A rounded walk has new vertices, so one hit gave the whole pass back to plain chords.

This PR changes the law for corner arcs only. The decision is in `docs/decisions/2317-blend-crossing-law.md`.

1. `machining2d/blend_cross.rs` (new): the law keeps the walks as fitted and rounds them again each round.
   - A corner arc that crosses another feed bans its own corner. The corner stays sharp. The fillet note counts it: "an arc there would cross another feed".
   - A fitted arc that crosses goes back to the chords of the plan, through `arc_cross::refuse` on the fitted walks.
   - After `CROSS_ROUNDS` (3) rounds no corner is rounded and the classic law holds on the fitted walks.
2. `machining2d/arc_touch.rs` (new): a tangent touch of a corner arc is not a crossing. A chord `q` is a touch when it stays within `d` of the tangent line at an end of the arc, over the reach of the bracket, and `d + dr <= 1e-5 mm`. `dr` is the difference of the two end radii.
3. `machining2d/fillet.rs`: `fillet_corners_except` takes the banned corners and returns the trace of each added or trimmed arc. `fillet_corners` is a wrapper with no ban.
4. `machining2d/pocket_emit.rs`: with corner arcs on and the law in force, the pocket calls the new loop.

## Proof bound of the touch

A circle lies on one side of each of its tangents. The last edge of the circumscribed hull lies on the tangent at the end. Thus each bracket point `X` holds `(X - E) . n <= dr`. Thus the true arc passes `q` by `d + dr <= 1e-5 mm` at most. The allowance can hide no crossing deeper than 0.01 micrometer. A pair that cannot be measured (no finite radius, an empty clip, a NaN) is a crossing.

A tolerance in the general predicate was dropped: it has no proof bound at a shared vertex. Adaptive (HSM) and `machining3d::hsm` pass an empty set of corner arcs, so their result is the same as before.

## Readings

Fixture of `corner_arc_radius` (pocket with an island, 8 mm tool):

| Case | Corner arcs kept | Corners refused for a crossing | `crossed_pairs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waterline, 1 mm | 12 of 31 | 0 | empty |
| Waterline, tool radius | 22 of 45 | 4 | empty |
| Offset rings, 1 mm | 35 of 38 | 0 | empty |
| Offset rings, tool radius | 31 of 38 | 0 | empty |

Without the touch allowance (experiment, not committed): 1 Waterline corner and 2 Offset rings corners at 1 mm lose their arc for a touch.

## Tests

Pinning tests in `crates/motion/tests/corner_arc_radius.rs`:

- `the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere` (new)
- `corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` (now reports each strategy that fails)
- unit tests `only_a_chord_on_the_end_tangent_is_a_touch` and `a_radius_mismatch_past_the_bound_leaves_no_touch` in `arc_touch.rs`

Run on head `79ea4410d22bda122207e9624123c31bfedd95fb`, debug, all pass:

- `camcraft-motion --lib` (405), `corner_arc_radius` (8), `corner_blend` (14), `corner_blend_arc` (9), `corner_blend_arc_contour` (1), `machining2d` (68), `rest2d` (13), `rest_zigzag` (2), `level_links` (12), `xy_arc_entry` (5), `entry_arc` (12)
- HSM and Adaptive: `adaptive_band` (2), `adaptive_hsm` (2), `adaptive_orbit_seam` (1), `pocket3d_hsm` (3), `pocket3d_mask_edge` (4), `machining3d` (23), `cross_invariance` (2), `optimal_load` (4), `pocket_refusal` (3), `predrilled_entry` (6)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `camcraft-app --test golden_cl` (33): pass, no golden moved

## Output that changes

Pocket operations with corner arcs on, with strategy Waterline or Offset rings (also as the fallback of Adaptive), or with `hold_crossings`: the corner arcs are back, less the corners that would cross. With corner arcs off, nothing changes.

## Not exercised

- The ignored (release lane) tests.
- The UI and the post processors. The bound is stated against the 1e-6 mm lattice of the CL data. The word format of each post script was not read.
- The fallback after `CROSS_ROUNDS` has no fixture that reaches it.
- Zigzag and Auto without `hold_crossings` post rounded walks with no crossing law, as before #2273. This PR does not change that.

Changelog: Pocket corner arcs are back for Waterline and Offset rings; a corner whose arc would cross another feed stays sharp and the note says so (#2317).

Effort: max

Fixes #2317

title: fix(post): refuse the post when the default machine file is missing or malformed
body:
## What changed

- `posting::default_machine_checked()` reads the default machine file (`assets/machines/3axis-vmc.mch`) as a `Result`. `parse_default_machine` refuses a file in these cases:
  - the file does not read;
  - the file is not JSON;
  - the file is not a JSON object;
  - the object has no `name` or no `kinematics.static` object. These are the keys that the post reads for the header and the coolant words. The shipped `3axis-vmc.mch` has both.
- The code is in the new module `crates/app/src/posting_default_machine.rs` (59 lines), not in `posting.rs`. `posting.rs` goes from 1547 to 1535 lines. #2322 tracks the full split.
- A refusal is not kept until restart. Only a machine that passed the check is kept (`posting::KeptMachine`). `default_mch_text` reads at each call and keeps nothing. A failed read or a refused file is read again at the next post, so a repaired file posts without a restart.
- `posting_mounts::posted_machine_for` is the one door from a mount to the engine's machine value. A mounted machine is mirrored as before. No mounted machine reads `default_machine_checked()` and refuses with `post blocked - ...`.
- The three post paths use it: the single-file post (`post_script_body_with`), the per-mount post (`post_each`) and the per-operation post.
- `default_machine()` keeps its `Value` form for the sim traverse clock (it writes no G-code).
- `engine::run` with `Value::Null` stays a legal input (the `post` binary, the script check in `commands/post.rs`, the tests).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2319-default-machine-refusal.md`.

## Readings

Before the fix, with no default machine file or a malformed file, the CLI exits 0 and writes a complete program. Compared with the good file, the header reads `O0001 (CAMCRAFT)` in place of `O0001 (VMC 3-AXIS)`, and all `M8` / `M9` lines are gone. The issue comment has the details.

After the fix, the CLI exits 1 and writes no file. The messages are:
- `post blocked - the default machine file 3axis-vmc.mch cannot be read (<reason>) - mount a machine on the setup, or reinstall the file`
- `post blocked - the default machine file 3axis-vmc.mch is malformed (<parse error> | not a machine object | it has no machine name | it has no kinematics.static section) - mount a machine on the setup, or reinstall the file`

The per-mount post puts the mount label in front (for example `Setup2: post blocked - ...`). The per-operation post puts the operation name in front (`Face2: post blocked - ...`).

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/default_machine_missing.rs` (9 tests). The CLI tests spawn the real CLI beside a hand-made `assets/` folder:
- `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post`
- `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_mount`: Setup1 mounted, Setup2 not mounted. Exit 1, names `Setup2` and the file, the output folder stays empty.
- `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation`: the same document, one file per operation. Exit 1, names `Face2` and the file, the output folder stays empty.
- `a_malformed_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post`
- `an_empty_object_as_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post` (`{}`)
- `a_good_default_machine_file_still_posts` (control, with `M8`)
- `the_default_machine_file_must_be_a_machine_object` (unit: `[]`, `"x"`, `null`, `{}`, a blank name, no `kinematics.static`, a `static` array, an unreadable file)
- `a_repaired_default_machine_file_is_read_again_and_a_good_one_is_kept` (unit: missing, then `{}`, then the good file give Err, Err, Ok; a later `{}` gives the kept machine)
- `the_shipped_default_machine_file_is_accepted` (unit)

Mutations, each reverted after the run:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `post_each` reads `machine_value_for` (null machine) again | `..._per_mount` fails |
| The per-operation post reads `machine_value_for` again | `..._per_operation` fails |
| The file text is kept as soon as it reads (the old caching) | `a_repaired_..._is_kept` fails |
| `parse_default_machine` accepts any object | `an_empty_object_...` and `the_default_machine_file_must_be_a_machine_object` fail |

Other targeted suites, all green: `golden_cl` (33), `post_not_judged` (4), `shipped_from_disk` (3), `solid_law_goldens` (7), `posting` (17), `per_op_files` (9), `per_op_script_options` (2), `setup_mounts_post` (8). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Follow-up issues

- #2321: the post does not check the default machine's limits for a document with no mounted machine (older gap, `P3`).
- #2322: split `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (`P7`).

## Not exercised

- The GUI post dialog and the MCP post tools. They call the same app post functions, but no test drives them here.
- The re-read is tested through `KeptMachine` with a given reader, not through a running CLI process.
- A default file with a name and a `kinematics.static` section but no limits still posts with the engine defaults (#2321).
- No release build, no wasm build.

Changelog: A missing or malformed default machine file now refuses the post with a message that names the file. Before, the post wrote a program with no coolant words and no machine name.

Effort: high

Fixes #2319

title: fix(post): find the repository assets under the new cargo build-dir layout
body:
## What changed

`camcraft_post::data_dir::cargo_profile_dir` (`crates/post/src/data_dir.rs`) now accepts the old and the new cargo build-dir layout.

- Old layout (no change): the exe is in `target/<profile>` or in its `deps` / `examples` child. The profile folder holds `.fingerprint`.
- New layout: a test exe is in `target/<profile>/build/<pkg>/<hash>/out`. The function maps it to `target/<profile>`. A profile folder that holds `build/camcraft-post` is a cargo build tree. This marker also applies to the uplifted binaries in `target/<profile>`.

An installed exe without its `assets/<kind>` folder is still refused by name. The decision is in `docs/decisions/2316-data-dir-new-layout.md`.

## Readings (run 43990986558, `gate-logs` artifact)

```
     Running unittests src/lib.rs (target/debug/build/camcraft-post/4d4a6b2fbedf41a7/out/camcraft_post-4d4a6b2fbedf41a7)
no posts folder found - the program needs its assets/posts directory beside the executable (looked in: /home/ghrunner/runner-work/Camcraft/Camcraft/target/debug/build/camcraft-post/4d4a6b2fbedf41a7/out/assets/posts)
```

Each "looked in" list in the logs has one path only. This includes `target/debug/assets/posts` for the uplifted `camcraft-cli`. Thus `target/debug/.fingerprint` does not exist on the runner.

## Pinning test

`data_dir::tests::the_new_cargo_build_dir_layout_finds_the_repository_assets` (camcraft-post lib). It uses the exe paths of the runner log. It fails without the fix (`left: []`) and passes with the fix, on Windows.

## Tests (Windows, cargo 1.99.0, `-j 6`, `--test-threads=6`)

- `camcraft-post` lib: 76 passed (11 `data_dir` tests).
- `camcraft-app` `shipped_from_disk`: 3 passed.
- `camcraft-app` `golden_cl`: 33 passed.
- `camcraft-app` `post_not_judged`: 4 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The local cargo (1.99.0) uses the old layout. I could not run a real build in the new layout on Windows. The pinning test copies the paths of the runner log, but the real layout is proved only by the next post-merge run.
- `camcraft-motion` `corner_arc_radius` also fails on that run. It is a different defect and it fails on Windows too. It is tracked in #2317, not here.

Changelog: Test executables and dev runs find the shipped posts and machine files with the new cargo build-dir layout.

Effort: high

Fixes #2316

title: fix(sim): a stock-source Deburr that cuts into a part never posts
body:
The base is now `main`.

## What changed

- `stock_sim::breaks::breaks_stock_edge` now includes a Deburr whose source is the setup's stock. The program sim gives its bevel no edge-break credit (#303) over a part's columns.
- `keep_law::is_stock_kept_kind` now includes Deburr. At generation the solid law keeps the cut out of each part of the setup. The post's live re-judge names a part that is added after generation.
- New function `stock_sim::breaks::stock_part_of`. It finds a from-model stock whose facets equal a judged part in place (vertex for vertex, 1e-6). That stock IS the part. A Deburr off that stock keeps the credit, and `parts_in_stock` / `kept_models` spare that one part. All other parts stay kept.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2313-stock-deburr-credit.md`.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/stock_deburr_part.rs`)

- `a_stock_source_deburr_into_a_part_known_at_generation_never_posts`: about 1 mm into "other", on aligned stock and on stock turned a quarter about Z. The op has a blocking gouge, and the post refuses with the sim's gouge line.
- `a_part_added_under_a_stock_source_deburr_is_refused_by_name`: 1 mm and 0.05 mm, aligned and quarter turn. The setup posts before the part is added. After that, the post refuses with "S1 now cuts part 'other'".
- `a_stock_source_deburr_clear_of_every_part_still_posts`: aligned and quarter turn.
- `a_deburr_of_the_parts_own_edge_still_posts`: a part source, and a stock source on a from-model stock.

## Mutations

- All `src` changes reverted: the first two tests fail (no gouge at generation; the setup posts after the part is added).
- `stock_part_of` forced to `None`: only `a_deburr_of_the_parts_own_edge_still_posts` fails. The from-model exemption carries load.

## Readings (debug, `-p camcraft-app`, `--test-threads=6`)

All pass:
- `stock_deburr_part` 4
- `stock_chamfer_added_part` 3
- `edge_break_gate` 5
- `edge_break_bound` 5
- `stock_source_holes` 9
- `keep_law` 31
- `kept_parts_live` 4
- `post_not_judged` 4
- `golden_cl` 33
- `deburr_links` 1
- `edge_volume_bound` 2
- `setup_carry_credits` 7
- `setup_align_2d_kinds` 8
- `stock_source_cross_drill` 6
- `operations` filtered to `deburr`: 5

`cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- For a part known at generation, the post line does not name the part. The refusal is the sim's located gouge plus the op's own blocking gouge finding.
- A stock that the sim cannot judge (an odd turn): only the live re-judge acts. No test covers it here.
- This change is stricter in one case. A stock-source Deburr on a box stock, or on a from-model stock moved off its source, now takes the solid law. If its cone reaches a part, the result is a gouge. The workaround is a part source. No existing test had this case.
- No full suite run and no GUI run.

## Review fix (head after 820245b9b)

- New finding `Warning::StockDeburrGouge` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`). Text: `move N cuts past the finish surface (stock-source deburr breaks into a part; use the part as source)`. `keep_law::note_stock_chamfer_gouges` writes it for a stock-source Deburr. MCP reports it as `gouge`.
- When the sim gouge verdict blocks the post, the post line now also names the convicted op and the part (`posting_sim::stock_edge_named`, `kept_rejudge::stock_edge_problem`): `... - S1 breaks into part 'other' (move N cuts past the finish surface (stock-source deburr breaks into a part; use the part as source))`.
- The live re-judge of a part added after generation says the Deburr way out.
- New pin `a_from_model_stock_moved_off_its_part_is_not_the_part`: a from-model stock moved 0.5 mm in X, aligned and turned a quarter about Z. The stock-source Deburr is refused.
- `a_stock_source_deburr_into_a_part_known_at_generation_never_posts` now asserts the op name, the part name and the way out in the post line.
- Mutation: `stock_part_of` without the facet check makes the new pin fail. Mutation: no `stock_edge_named` makes the known-part pin and the new pin fail.
- Readings: `stock_deburr_part` 5, `stock_chamfer_added_part` 3, `keep_law` 31, `kept_parts_live` 4, `edge_break_gate` 5, `post_not_judged` 4, `stock_source_holes` 9, `camcraft-sim` lib 184: all pass. Clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets` and `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets`, `-D warnings`: clean.
- Not exercised: a raw-stock-only or fixture source for the from-model exception (the code refuses the exception there; no test).

Changelog: A Deburr with the stock as its source that cuts into a part is now refused at the post and names the operation and the part; a Deburr on a from-model stock that is the part still posts.

Effort: high

Fixes #2313

title: fix(sim): a stock-source chamfer's bevel is no credit over a part
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/src/stock_sim_breaks.rs`: new `breaks_stock_edge(world, op)`. It is true for a 2D Chamfer whose source names the setup's stock (the stock, or picks off the stock).
- `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` (`plan_program`): the program sim credits no edge-break record of such an op. A part under the stock's edge is judged sharp.
- `crates/app/src/posting_sim.rs` (`judge_clause`):
  - Gouge arm: the refusal also gets the `kept_moved` line (#1628), so it names the op and the part.
  - Clean arm (review finding 1): when every op is covered, the gate runs `kept_moved` too. A cut too shallow for the sim's lattice is thus refused by name.
- `docs/decisions/2308-stock-chamfer-no-credit.md`: the decision, the dropped options and the cost. It names #2313 for the stock-source Deburr gouge, which this PR does not fix.
- The branch has `origin/main` at `3f41b8da6` (#2309) merged, with no conflicts.

## Cause

1. The #303 credit took the declared bevel of the stock's edge as part of the finished part, over all columns under that edge.
2. A part added after generation under that edge was thus judged as bevelled. The sim found zero gouge cells.
3. With a clean sim verdict, the live re-judge (`kept_moved`) did not run, and `G01 X35. Y-35. Z19.` posted along the edge of the added part.

The #1631 solid law forbids a stock-source chamfer to enter any part. No refusal, gouge check or collision check is removed or made weaker. The sim verdict stays a judge. The live re-judge is an added judge in the clean arm.

## Readings

- On `main`, the aligned 1 mm case posts with `G01 X35. Y-35. Z19.`. With the fix, aligned and quarter-turned stock are refused by the sim gouge plus `S1 now cuts part 'other' (... stock-source chamfer breaks into a part ...)`. The hair-turned stock (not judged by the sim) is refused by `kept_moved`.
- A part added 0.05 mm into the chamfer's cut (x 30..34.05): with only the no-credit change it POSTED (mutation check on this head). With the clean-arm re-judge, it is refused by name on aligned and quarter-turned stock.
- A part added clear of the cut (x 18..24) posts on all three turns.

## Pinning tests

- `stock_chamfer_added_part::a_part_added_under_a_judged_stock_source_chamfer_is_refused_by_name` (aligned, quarter, hair; 1 mm cut)
- `stock_chamfer_added_part::a_part_added_a_hair_under_a_judged_stock_source_chamfer_is_refused_by_name` (aligned, quarter; 0.05 mm cut)
- `stock_chamfer_added_part::a_part_added_clear_of_a_stock_source_chamfer_still_posts` (aligned, quarter, hair)

## Suites on head `498ba08b5` (debug, `-j 6 --test-threads=6`)

All green:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `stock_chamfer_added_part` | 3 passed |
| `stock_source_holes` | 9 passed |
| `keep_law` | 31 passed |
| `kept_parts_live` | 4 passed |
| `edge_break_gate` | 5 passed |
| `edge_break_bound` | 5 passed |
| `circular_pick_law` | 5 passed |
| `trochoid_law` | 7 passed |
| `pocket3d_open_side` | 7 passed |
| `post_not_judged` | 4 passed |
| `setup_carry_credits` | 7 passed |
| `setup_align_2d_kinds` | 8 passed |
| `mill2d_b` | 9 passed |
| `stock_source_cross_drill` | 6 passed |
| `golden_cl` | 33 passed |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt -p camcraft-app -- --check`: clean.

No legal program becomes refused: each "posts" case in the suites above still posts, the part-source chamfer and deburr of `edge_break_gate` included.

## Order of refusal lines

On sim-judged stock, a stock-source chamfer that cuts a part deep enough for the lattice is refused by the sim gouge first, then the op line. After #2309, the `stock_source_holes` chamfer cases turn the stock 1e-6 rad, where the sim does not judge. No assert in this PR was changed for the order.

## Not exercised

- No run on a real control.
- No GUI run, no full workspace build, no release lanes, no heavy lanes.
- A stock-source Deburr that cuts a part still posts. That is #2313, also on `main`, and not in this PR.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer off the stock no longer posts when a part added after generation stands under the stock's edge, also for a cut of a few hundredths of a millimetre; the post refuses and names the operation and the part.

Effort: high

Fixes #2308

## What changed

A new built-in post **LinuxCNC** (`assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`, extension `.ngc`) and a generic machine **LinuxCNC 3-axis** (`assets/machines/linuxcnc-3axis.mch`). The post uses the RS274NGC dialect from the public LinuxCNC 2.9 G-code and M-code references. Its structure comes from our own `tormach.cps`. The PathPilot assumptions are removed: no "machine Z0 is the top" convention, no G30 before each tool change, no belt-range notes, no 1-1000 tool range, no 4th axis.

Post options (declared, so the UI, CLI and MCP show them):

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `retractMode` | `g53` (`G53 G0 Z<safe_retract>`), `g28` / `g30` (`G91 G28 Z0` + `G90`, Z only), `none` | `g53` |
| `writeToolLength` | `G43 H<n>` after `T<n> M6`; off when the M6 remap applies the length (the section `G49` is then left out too) | on |
| `pathControl` / `blendTolerance` | `G64 P<tol>` (mm, written in the program unit) or `G61` | `G64 P0.025` |
| `programEnd` | `M30` or `M2` | `M30` |
| `percentDelimiters` | `%` on the first and the last line | off |

Also: safe start block `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G49 G80`, no O word, comments in parentheses (active keywords made inert), `S M3`, `M7`/`M8`/`M9` from the machine coolant list (`PARAM Coolant` read), arcs and helices with incremental IJK (or the R-arc option), G73/G81/G82/G83/G85/G86/G89 with G99, G38.2/G38.3 probing as in the PathPilot post.

Base: upstream main `fac6c8e8d` (not a cut tag: the fork main is behind v0.22.0, and this PR targets upstream main).

Tapping:
- A rigid tap is `G33.1 Z<bottom> K<pitch>` (pitch = feed / rpm). The post writes it only when the machine file states `rigid_tapping: true` (the reference requires a spindle encoder). Else it refuses by name.
- A floating-holder tap is `G84 ... F<rpm x pitch>` (the reference says G84 is not spindle-synchronized). The post declares `floatingTapping = true`.

Refused by name: `G53` retract with no stated `safe_retract` (no machine included, #435 / #495), control compensation (G41/G42), tilted moves, a trip home after an operation, tool numbers that are not positive whole numbers, G73/G83 with Q <= 0.

Engine: the machine mirror read an unstated `rigid_tapping` as `rigidTapping: true` (the unstated-limit law). The post must not take that as "an encoder is present". So the engine now also publishes `machine.rigidTappingStated` (true only for a stated `rigid_tapping: true`). No other post reads it. `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents it.

Registration: `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES` (`crates/app/src/posting.rs`), the post-name lists in `cam.d.ts` and `script/mod.rs`, README, `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`. Decisions: `docs/decisions/2303-linuxcnc-post.md`.

## How it was tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/linuxcnc_post.rs` (9 tests): registry and library; unstated safe Z refused, never `G53 G0 Z0`; stated safe Z before `M6`, after `G43` and at the end; `G28`/`G30`/none retracts; no `G43`/section `G49` with the remap option; `G61`, `M2`, `%`, inch blend tolerance, end units; rigid tap refused without an encoder and `G33.1 Z-12 K1.5` with one (inch `K0.059055`); floating tap `G84`; tilted move and control compensation refused. Every program is checked to hold only G/M words from the LinuxCNC reference.
- `conformance`: new goldens `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/linuxcnc/*.nc` (12) and `synth_linuxcnc.nc`; `tap_plate` is a named refusal on the generic VMC (no encoder stated); extension `.ngc` pinned.
- `script_linuxcnc` (post binary on the recorded streams, goldens in `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/linuxcnc/`). These are machine-less, so each case is the named safe-Z refusal (or the 3-axis refusal).
- Cross-post lists extended: `cycle_hop` (hop law, run with `retractMode=g30`), `ream_cycle`, `comp`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post_spindle_rule_all`, `machine`.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, head 95b83ca24, macOS): 579 steps, 573 green. The 6 red suites are exactly the 18 tests that #2306 lists as red on this base (`fac6c8e8d`, main is red after batch 16): `circular_pick_law`, `keep_law`, `kept_parts_live`, `pocket3d_open_side`, `stock_source_holes`, `trochoid_law`. None of them posts through this post.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` and clippy on the new and changed app test targets: clean.

## Not exercised

- Not run in a LinuxCNC sim or on a machine. The reporter (sn3ro) offered a LinuxCNC 2.9 sim run and an air cut.
- G33.1 and G84 behaviour on a real spindle; the `none` retract with a real M6 remap.
- Control compensation (G41/G42) is refused, not written. A 4th axis is not supported.

Changelog: New LinuxCNC 3-axis mill post and generic machine: retract by G53 safe Z, G28/G30 or none; optional G43 after a remapped M6; G64 P or G61; G33.1 rigid tap only with a stated spindle encoder, G84 for floating holders (#2303)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #2303

title: fix(test): six refusal suites take the oblique not-judged device
body:
## What changed

#2182 (#2177) makes the program sim judge a box stock that is turned a quarter about Z. This change is correct and on purpose (`docs/decisions/2177-square-stock-sim.md`). #2182 changed four suites that used the quarter turn as the device "the sim does not judge". Six other suites kept that device. Their checks that the operation's own clause holds the post saw the sim's gouge clause first. Thus 18 tests in `camcraft-app` went red on main (post-merge run 43977363817).

This PR changes only tests:

- `circular_pick_law`, `trochoid_law`, `keep_law`, `kept_parts_live`, `stock_source_holes`, `pocket3d_open_side` turn the stock 1e-6 rad about Z (`OBLIQUE`), the device of #2177.
- `pocket_support` gets `stock_turn`, `OBLIQUE` and `oblique_refused`, the twins of the `area_support` helpers.
- Each check that the operation's own clause holds the post now also asserts that the sim refuses the stock by name (`stock_follow::OBLIQUE_STOCK`).
- The fixture box checks take 1e-4 mm in X and Y. Z stays at 1e-9.

No "never posts" assert is removed. No refusal, gouge check or collision check changes.

## Readings

On `7e26134bf` without this change:

- 17 tests: the post is still refused. The sim clause leads, for example `post blocked - gouge: program cuts below the model in 4695 cell(s), worst 3.00 mm`.
- 1 test (`stock_source_chamfer_refusal_names_cause_and_part_as_source_workaround`, case "chamfer-rejudge-hint"): the program POSTED. A stock-source 2D Chamfer cuts into a part that was added after generation. The same case also posts with an aligned stock, since #1628. The cause is in `posting_sim::judge_clause`: the live re-judge runs only when the sim does not judge. This PR does not fix that defect. It is #2308 (P1). With the oblique device, this suite again pins the re-judge where the sim does not judge.

## Pinning tests

All tests of the six suites pass with this change:

- `circular_pick_law`: 5 passed
- `trochoid_law`: 7 passed
- `keep_law`: 31 passed
- `kept_parts_live`: 4 passed
- `stock_source_holes`: 9 passed
- `pocket3d_open_side`: 7 passed

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The other suites that include `pocket_support` were compiled by clippy but not run. Their code is unchanged; the new helpers are additions.
- No batch gate, no UI suites, no release lanes.
- `pocket3d_open_side.rs` was 423 lines before this PR and is 422 lines now. It stays over the 400-line law; a split is not in this fix.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2306-red-refusal-suites.md`.

Effort: high (no escalation).

title: feat(post): add clean-room Mach4 milling postprocessor
body:
Stacked on #2162 (merge #2162 first)

## What changed
- Added the clean-room Mach4 milling postprocessor in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`.
- Left 3-axis programs in `G94` mode with `G20`/`G21` unit blocks, `G90 G94 G91.1 G40 G49 G17 G64` safety header, `G17`/`G18`/`G19` arcs, `G41`/`G42`/`G40` cutter compensation, `G54`..`G59` and `G54.1 P1`..`P248` work offsets, `G28`/`G53`/`G30` safe retracts, `G73`/`G81`/`G82`/`G83`/`G84`/`G85`/`G86`/`G89` canned cycles with decimal-second `P` dwells, and `G31` Macro B probing.
- Added 3+2 indexed AC trunnion support in `G94` (no `G43.4` or `G93`) using `#1962`'s trunnion schema (`A` parent of `C`, `pivot`, `offset`, `zeroOffset`, `rollover`, `signConvention`, `controller.rtcp = false`).
- Added analytical AC inverse kinematics, platter-center G54 datum transform (`work_datum = a_pivot + c_offset`), rotated cardinal arc projection, optional paired `rotaryUnclamp`/`rotaryClamp` M-codes, and safe-retract-only `C` rollover handling (`rollover_360` vs `unwrapped`).
- Added named refusals when `controller.rtcp` is `true`, when AC trunnion geometry or travel bounds are invalid or missing, or when an indexed section changes tool orientation during cutting (`"needs #1966: inverse-time feed"`).
- Registered `"Mach4"` in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and added `"Mach4"` conformance and script entries in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` and `crates/post/tests/script_mach4.rs`.
- Documented unattended choices in `docs/decisions/1968-mach4-post.md`.

## Cause
Camcraft shipped no Mach4 milling dialect, and Mach4 controllers lack native Fanuc `G43.4` RTCP while `#1966` (`G93` inverse-time feed) is not yet merged.

## Tests
- Pins added (all failed red before implementation):
  - `crates/post/tests/mach4_post.rs` (3 tests: 3-axis mm/inch dialect words and cycles, `G31` probing, `G53`/`G30` safe retracts)
  - `crates/post/tests/mach4_trunnion.rs` (3 tests: mm/inch `table_rh`/`tool_rh` 3+2 kinematics verified via `forward_part`, rollover `[0, 360)` and clamp M-code ordering, RTCP/trunnion-geometry/simultaneous refusals)
  - `crates/app/tests/mach4_builtin.rs` (2 tests: `BUILTINS` + `post_serves`, end-to-end `post_setup` on `3axis-vmc.mch`)
  - `crates/post/tests/script_mach4.rs` (`post_suite!("mach4.cps")`, 11 recorded cases)
- Mutation checks verified (each turned pinning tests red, then returned green on restore):
  - Removed `"Mach4"` from `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`: `mach4_builtin` failed (`0 passed; 2 failed`).
  - Bypassed `m.rtcp === true` check in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`: `mach4_refuses_rtcp_bad_trunnion_and_simultaneous_by_name` failed.
  - Bypassed simultaneous mid-section orientation guard in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`: `mach4_refuses_rtcp_bad_trunnion_and_simultaneous_by_name` failed.
  - Bypassed `cRollover` wrapping in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`: `mach4_rotary_rollover_unwrapped_vs_360_and_clamp_order` failed.
  - Bypassed missing `A.pivot` guard in `assets/posts/mach4.cps`: `mach4_refuses_rtcp_bad_trunnion_and_simultaneous_by_name` failed.
- Checks run after final edit:
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green (0 warnings).
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (`post` 17s, `motion` 1166s, `app` 2067s, `ui` 303s; 4 steps, 0 failed).

## Goldens moved
- Zero existing `.nc` or `.cl` goldens changed (`git diff --stat base-2162 -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).
- Added 14 new Mach4 conformance goldens: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_mach4.nc` and 13 `.nc` files under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/mach4/`.
- Added 11 new `mach4.cps` recorded script verdicts under `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/mach4/` (7 `.nc`, 4 `.refusal`).

## Not exercised
- No physical Mach4 controller hardware run or Mach4 simulator GUI verification ran in CI; Mach4 syntax and RS-274 rules rest on public documentation and `camcraft_post::kinematics::forward_part` round-trips.
- Simultaneous 4/5-axis `G93` inverse-time cutting waits for `#1966` and refuses by name until then.

## Overlaps
- Stacked on `#2162` (`issue/1962-trunnion-schema`) for `#1962` AC trunnion fields and kinematics (`base-2162`).
- Open PRs `#2293`, `#2290`, `#2253`, `#2149`, and `#2136` touch other parts of `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and not `BUILTINS` (`posting.rs` `BUILTINS` touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes).

Changelog: Add clean-room Mach4 milling postprocessor with 3-axis G94 and 3+2 AC trunnion support.
Fixes #1968

title: fix(post,app): read post scripts and machine files from disk at run time
body:
## What changed

- New module `crates/post/src/data_dir.rs`. It finds `assets/<kind>` at run time. The first directory that exists is used for the whole kind:
  1. `<exe dir>/assets/<kind>` (zip, installer, Linux tarball, deb/rpm, AppImage, flatpak, snap)
  2. `<app>/Contents/Resources/assets/<kind>` (macOS bundle)
  3. `<exe dir>/../../assets/<kind>` (dev run from `target/<profile>/`)
  4. `crates/post/../../assets/<kind>` (test binaries; a path, not a compiled-in copy)
- Candidates 3 and 4 apply only when the exe is in a cargo build tree. The marker is cargo's `.fingerprint` folder in the exe folder, or in the folder above `deps` / `examples`. An installed exe without its `assets/<kind>` folder gets the named refusal. It never reads the build machine's checkout, `/usr/assets` or `C:/assets`.
- There is no per-user `assets` folder. It could replace the shipped or repository files with no warning (review of this PR).
- New file `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`. `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES` now hold the file name (`AssetFile`), not the text. `builtin_post_text`, `builtin_machine_text` and `default_mch_text` read each file one time into a static cell and give `&'static str`. There is no leak.
- A missing directory, or a file that is missing, not UTF-8 or larger than 4 MiB, is an error. The error names the file and the directory. There is no compiled-in fallback on the desktop.
- The `wasm32` build has no disk. It keeps a compiled-in copy.
- Each read writes the full file path to the log one time. A user can see which post file made a program.
- The callers in `posting.rs`, `posting_serves.rs`, `load_machine.rs`, `setup_mount.rs` and `machine/library.rs` use the new functions. The test files use them or `posting::shipped_posts()` / `posting::shipped_machines()`.
- Themes: already read from disk (`crates/ui/src/theme_dir.rs`). No change.
- Scripts: `assets/scripts` was never compiled in. No change.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2282-assets-from-disk.md`.

## Packaging

No change to packaging, `build.rs` or workflows. The v0.22.0 Windows zip already has this layout:

```
camcraft-0.22.0-win-x64/
  assets/
    machines/   (39 .mch)
    posts/      (16 .cps)
    scripts/
    themes/
    ui/
  camcraft-cli.exe
  camcraft-ui.exe
  post.exe
  LICENSE
  NOTICE
  RELEASE_NOTES.md
  TESTING.md
```

`xtask/src/release_pack.rs` `ASSET_DIRS` and `scripts/package-*.sh` put the same `assets/` directories beside the executable on all platforms.

## Readings and pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` lib `data_dir::tests` (10 tests): order in a cargo tree, an installed exe without `assets` is refused (`an_installed_exe_without_assets_is_refused_not_redirected`), beside the exe wins, macOS bundle, missing directory error, missing file error, edited file loads and the read is cached, non-UTF-8 refusal, the 4 MiB cap (`a_file_over_the_size_cap_is_refused_by_name`), dev run finds the repository `assets`.
- `camcraft-app` lib `posting::files::the_browser_list_matches_the_disk_tables`: each `BUILTINS` / `MACHINES` file and the default machine are in the `wasm32` `embedded()` list, with the same text as on disk.
- `camcraft-app` `tests/shipped_from_disk.rs` (3 tests): each shipped post is the file on disk that `builtin_post_path` names; each machine reads; an unknown name is refused by name.
- Review-fix head: `camcraft-post` lib 75 passed; `posting` 17 passed; `shipped_from_disk` 3 passed. The other binaries in this list passed on the first head and were not run again: `machine`, `machine_library`, `post_serves_kind`, `tinyg_post`, `grblhal_post`, `smoothing`, `explain_option`, `wire_post`, `sodick_alc400g`, `tormach_machines`, the `lathe_voice` lib tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the review-fix head.

## Not exercised

- The `wasm32` build: `flecs_ecs_sys` does not build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` on this machine.
- The other changed test binaries were compiled (clippy `--all-targets`) but not run. Their changes are mechanical lookups.
- A packaged executable was not started.
- The post dialog does not show the post file path yet. Follow-up: #2292.
- Open PRs that add posts or machines to `posting.rs` (for example #2290, #2253, #2162) will conflict on the tables. Their new entries must use `AssetFile("<file>")` and the `wasm32` `embedded` list. The test `the_browser_list_matches_the_disk_tables` fails if the list misses one.

Changelog: The shipped post scripts and machine files are read from the assets folder beside the program at run time, so an edit there takes effect after a restart of the program, without a rebuild; a missing file is refused by name.

Effort: high

Fixes #2282

title: fix(sim): play the stock up to the first operation with no toolpath
body:
Stacked on #2192 (base `issue/2181-sim-precalc`). Retarget this PR to `main` before #2192 merges.

## What changed

- The stock playback (the transport's traced stock) plays the program in posting order up to the first operation that has no toolpath. It stops there. It does not skip that operation to cut the operations after it.
  - `posting::program_ops_until_ungenerated` and `stock_sim::plan_program_until_ungenerated` are new. Only `PlaySeed::gather` uses them.
  - `posting::program_ops` and `stock_sim::plan_program` keep their behaviour. The post and the Deviate verdict still refuse the program by name ("<op>: no toolpath yet - generate it first").
  - `PlayIndex::stop()` names the operation. `PlayIndex::position_at` holds the stock at the end of the plan when the playhead is on an operation at or after the stop.
  - When the first operation has no toolpath, the playback shows the uncut stock of that operation's setup.
- A separate line under the transport bar names the stop: "Stock simulation stops before 2D Contour1: it has no toolpath. Generate it to see the rest." (`play_precalc::stop_readout`, `play_precalc::transport_row`). The stop is not added to the status line. Thus the generation notes of a clean operation do not get the "!" error mark.
- The remaining playback refusal reads "stock simulation refused: <why> - the stock shows uncut". It replaces "traced playback refused: <why> - the sheet stands".
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2280-sim-partial-playback.md`.

## Safety

The stock judgment that can block the post does not change. `simulate_document`, `verification_gate` and the post walk `program_ops` as before. The pinning test asserts that `simulate_document` and `program_ops` still refuse the same document.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/stock_play_stop.rs`
  - `playback_plays_the_ops_before_the_first_one_without_a_toolpath`: the end of the playback equals the stock of the document with Face1 only; the verdict and the post still refuse.
  - `playback_never_skips_an_op_without_a_toolpath_to_cut_the_next`: the first operation has no toolpath; the generated second operation is not cut.
  - `a_whole_program_has_no_stop`.
- `crates/ui/src/play_precalc_tests.rs::an_op_without_a_toolpath_stops_the_playback_and_says_so`: the playback runs, the stop text is pinned, the status line is not changed.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/status_alert.rs::the_notes_of_a_clean_operation_are_not_an_alert`: the notes from the issue do not carry the error mark.
- Updated: `field_view_tests::a_refused_playback_is_said_once_and_retired_with_the_transport` (new refusal words).

## Readings

- app (`cargo test -p camcraft-app`): `stock_play_stop` 3 passed; `stock_play` 7 passed; `stock_play_precalc` 7 passed (1 ignored, heavy lane); `stock_sim_document` 9 passed.
- ui (`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, CWD `crates/ui`): `play_precalc` 3 passed; `status_alert` 5 passed; `field_view_tests` 3 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- All on head ba987e7b4.

## Not exercised

- The GUI was not started. The line under the transport bar was not seen on screen.
- The quick tier was not run; only the targeted tests above and clippy for `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`.
- `crates/ui/src/machined.rs` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/view_pass.rs` still say "the sheet stands" in two other refusals. They are not in the playback path of this issue.

Changelog: The stock simulation now plays up to the first operation that has no toolpath, and a separate line names that operation, instead of refusing the whole setup.

Effort: high

Fixes #2280

title: fix(3d): prevent shared-depth XY crossings in adaptive microlifts, helices, and offset shells
body:
## What changed

- Landed `entry::helix_about`'s final half-turn on exact `z1` and clamped intermediate `lattice` depths monotonically toward `z1` ([entry.rs](crates/motion/src/entry.rs)).
- Extracted shared depth-overlap and `CROSSING_TOUCH = 1e-9` segment-crossing checks (`z_depths_overlap`, `proper_cross_touch`, `seg_crosses_prior`, `moves_cross_prior`) in `machining2d::arc_cross` and re-exported them internally ([arc_cross.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/arc_cross.rs), [mod.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs)).
- Scaled `microlift::link_at` lift heights strictly below the nearest earlier horizontal `Feed` cut plane above `z`, probed candidate links against prior `Feed` moves, promoted crossing low links to `high: true` down-only links when clear, and fell back to a `hop_z` rapid plus `Plunge` retract when even `down` crosses or the gap is `<= 0.02 mm` ([microlift.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/microlift.rs)).
- Protected 3-D offset shells by probing `descent::push_helix` against posted `b.moves()` (re-placing around `along_pass`/`dive_room` or calling `fallback` when no bore clears) and hopping over any `level_ctx::feed_leg` chord that crosses a prior `Feed` move at shared depth or Z band ([descent.rs](crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs), [level_ctx.rs](crates/motion/src/machining3d/level_ctx.rs)).
- Added unit and integration pinning tests ([entry.rs](crates/motion/src/entry.rs), [microlift.rs](crates/motion/src/machining2d/microlift.rs), [pocket3d_mask_edge.rs](crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_mask_edge.rs)) and recorded the unattended design choices ([2237-pocket3d-mask-crossing.md](docs/decisions/2237-pocket3d-mask-crossing.md)).

## Cause

- `helix_about` snapped its last half-turn to `lattice(z1)` (`-0.45` vs `-0.44999999999999996`), leaving a 1-ULP ramp that overlapped the next level's descending helix (`min_hi - max_lo = 5.55e-17 > 0`).
- `microlift::link_at` applied `0.30..1.50 mm` lifts without checking the stepdown gap above `z` or whether candidate microlifts crossed same-level entry ramps/helices.
- `descent::bore_meets_lifted_leg` only checked `lvl.passes` at `pz`, missing lifted moves emitted by earlier levels into `b.moves()`.
- `level_ctx::feed_leg` emitted shifted `OffsetRings + shell` floor passes at `bottom_z` across `x/y` already cut by the penultimate level's `floor_z`-clamped pass at exact `bottom_z`.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `entry::tests::helix_about_exact_end_z_prevents_next_level_ulp_crossing` (red before fix, green after)
  - `machining2d::microlift::tests::microlift_link_stays_below_prior_level_and_avoids_entry_crossings` (red before fix, green after)
  - `adaptive_small_stepdown_microlift_and_helix_stay_crossing_free` in `pocket3d_mask_edge` (red before fix, green after)
  - `offset_shell_fillet_helix_and_floor_never_cross` in `pocket3d_mask_edge` (red before fix, green after)
- Mutations (each guard mutated individually back toward `upstream/main` -> red -> restored -> green):
  - `entry::helix_about` exact `z1` -> `[[2, 4]]` crossing -> restored green
  - `microlift::link_at` prior-level gap cap -> climbed to `+0.10` above `-0.15` -> restored green
  - `microlift::link_at` `try_prof` crossing probe -> failed on `same-level ramp crossing up leg` -> restored green
  - `level_ctx::feed_leg` `seg_crosses_prior` hop -> `[Crossing { moves: [865, 1032] }, Crossing { moves: [873, 1039] }]` -> restored green
  - `descent::push_helix` `probe_helix`/`find_clear_helix` -> `[Crossing { moves: [224, 355] }, Crossing { moves: [725, 856] }]` -> restored green
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed (`0` warnings).
- Gate (`quick`, `--base upstream/main` at `1b6e08182`): `cargo xtask gate quick` completed `[01] motion suites` (`ok in 2822s`: all `56` `camcraft-motion` unit + integration suites passed, `0` failed) before a host restart interrupted `[02] app suites`; `[02] app suites` was then run to completion with the exact quick-gate command (`51/51` `camcraft-app` integration suites passed, `0` failed; heavy `--ignored` suites skipped as usual).

## Goldens moved

- None (`git diff --stat -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- `~/sc-parts/sc_logo.camproj` itself (inaccessible in this worker sandbox; covered via synthetic multi-level small-stepdown Adaptive and floor-fillet `OffsetRings + shell` fixtures instead).
- Heavy `--ignored` release suites (`adaptive_hsm`, `rotary_adaptive`, `offset_shells`, `verify` envelope tests).

## Overlaps

- `#2035` (Draft, `conflicts` label) touches `crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs` (imports, `Ask`, `from`, `helix` -> `descent_place.rs`, `descend`), different functions from `push_helix`; whichever merges second refreshes.

Effort: high

Changelog: fix(3d): prevent shared-depth XY crossings in 3D pocket helices, adaptive microlifts, and offset-shell floors

Fixes #2237

title: fix(setup): generate the hole kinds, Circular, Slot and Trochoidal Slot in an aligned setup
body:
Stacked on #2279. Retarget this PR to `main` before #2279 merges.

## What changed
- `setup_align::verified_kind` accepts six more kinds: Drill, Bore, Thread, Circular, Trochoidal Slot and Slot. The refusal message lists them.
- Slot picks read the setup frame. `slot_bound_of`, `confine_slot` and `slot_from_picks` take the op's setup and use `setup_align::pose_in`. Before, they used `model::transform_of` (the model frame). In an unaligned setup, `pose_in` gives the model pose, so that path does not change.
- Two old tests used Circular as the refused example. They use 2D Chamfer now (with the `CM-0600-90` chamfer mill).
- The decision file `docs/decisions/2276-aligned-setup-kinds.md` has a second section.

## Readings
- Hole recognition (`operation::detect_holes`) reads the material of the op's setup through `setup_align::facets_in`. Thus the hole list of a turned setup is in the setup frame.
- Circular, Trochoidal Slot and typed Slot take their region and heights from `region_for_job` and `part_aabb_in`, in the setup frame.

## Pinning tests
`crates/app/tests/setup_align_hole_kinds.rs` (new): a plate with two holes, turned 90 degrees about X and then about Z.
- `turned_drill_finds_and_cuts_the_holes_of_the_baked_part`
- `turned_bore_finds_and_cuts_the_holes_of_the_baked_part`
- `turned_thread_finds_and_cuts_the_holes_of_the_baked_part`
- `a_hole_list_from_the_turned_setup_never_drills_the_part_as_modelled_silently`

`crates/app/tests/setup_align_2d_kinds.rs`:
- `turned_circular_cuts_like_the_baked_part`
- `turned_trochoidal_slot_cuts_like_the_baked_part`
- `turned_typed_slot_cuts_like_the_baked_part`
- `turned_picked_slot_fills_the_turned_face`
- `kinds_without_proof_stay_refused_in_a_turned_setup` (Probe, 2D Chamfer, Deburr)

Each turned case must verify clean, simulate with no gouge, and post the same program as the baked part. The part as modelled must cut a different path or refuse.

Also run, all green: `setup_align`, `opframe_picks`, `slot_pick_refusals`, `slot_picks`. Clippy `-D warnings` is clean on the lib and these test targets. `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

## Not exercised
- The quick tier as one run. I ran the touched suites one by one.
- Thread on external bosses. The test threads holes only.
- Circular and Trochoidal Slot from picks. The tests use typed coordinates.
- A picked Slot that cuts into material. The picked Slot test cuts in air above the part; the proof is the seeded XY.
- The UI panels in a turned setup.

## Kinds still refused
- 2D Chamfer: #2283
- Deburr: #2284
- Probe: #2285
- 5-axis and rotary kinds: #2286
- Non-mill machines: #2287

The verify check and the post gate do not change.

Changelog: Drill, Bore, Thread, Circular, Trochoidal Slot and Slot operations now generate in a setup that holds the part turned (part alignment); picked Slot faces and edges are read in the setup frame.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #2276

title: fix(ui): read setup part alignment in boundary_picks::extend_to_loop
body:
## What changed
- Added `operation::extend_to_loop_in(world, setup, picks)` in `crates/app/src/operation/boundary_picks.rs` and re-exported it in `crates/app/src/operation/mod.rs`.
- Replaced `model::transform_of` with `setup_align::pose_in(world, &e, setup)` inside `extend_to_loop_in`. Face normals now rotate into the setup's part-alignment frame, matching `OpFrame::pose_in_setup` in `selection.rs`.
- Updated `operation::extend_to_loop(world, picks)` to call `extend_to_loop_in` with `setup::active(world)`, matching the viewport's `view_pose`.
- Updated `boundary_draft::extend` in `crates/ui/src/boundary_draft.rs` and `edge_pick::take_loop` in `crates/ui/src/edge_pick.rs` to pass the operation's `setup` to `extend_to_loop_in`.
- Added decision note `docs/decisions/2216-extend-to-loop-setup-align.md`.

## Cause
`boundary_picks::extend_to_loop` read `model::transform_of(world, &e)` and ignored the setup's `part_alignment`. Pure Z turns and 180-degree X/Y flips keep `|n.z|` unchanged (`|-n.z| == |n.z|`), so they matched by coincidence. A 90-degree flip onto a side or a free angle tilts Z, so `extend_to_loop` picked the model-frame horizontal face instead of the setup-frame horizontal face.

## Tests
- `area_picks::extend_to_loop_reads_face_normals_in_the_setup_frame`: RED before fix on `[90.0, 0.0, 0.0]`; GREEN after fix for `180° X`, `90° Z`, `90° X`, `55° X`, active `Setup2`, and `extend_to_loop_in` with `Setup1` active.
- `boundary_picks::extend_to_loop_button_uses_the_operations_aligned_setup`: pins `boundary_draft::extend` on `Setup2` (`90° X`) while `Setup1` is active.
- `edge_loop_pick::shift_click_on_an_aligned_setup_closes_around_the_setup_horizontal_face`: pins `edge_pick::queue_edge_pick` with Shift on `Setup2` (`90° X`) while `Setup1` is active.
- Mutation 1 (revert `setup_align::pose_in` to `model::transform_of` in `extend_to_loop_in`): `area_picks::extend_to_loop_reads_face_normals_in_the_setup_frame` FAILS -> restored -> PASSES.
- Mutation 2 (revert `boundary_draft::extend` to `extend_to_loop`): `boundary_picks::extend_to_loop_button_uses_the_operations_aligned_setup` FAILS -> restored -> PASSES.
- Mutation 3 (revert `edge_pick::take_loop` to `extend_to_loop`): `edge_loop_pick::shift_click_on_an_aligned_setup_closes_around_the_setup_horizontal_face` FAILS -> restored -> PASSES.
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` PASSED (`wall 15.6 min, 2 step(s), 0 failed`: all 224 `camcraft-app` suites and all `camcraft-ui` suites).
- Clippy: `env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` PASSED (0 warnings).

## Goldens moved
None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` returned empty).

## Review visual evidence
Actual shell and GPU viewport captures from the same fixture, with Setup2 active and its part alignment rotated 90° about X. Before captures temporarily restore the old `model::transform_of` lookup; after captures use this PR head. The old lookup selects the vertical model-top face. The fix selects the horizontal face in the aligned setup. Both captures use the same camera and picked edge.

| Action | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Extend to loop | ![Extend before: vertical face loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1874a187aa3c58f81624f82571aa43aa317023e1/2281/extend-before.png) | ![Extend after: aligned horizontal face loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1874a187aa3c58f81624f82571aa43aa317023e1/2281/extend-after.png) |
| Shift-click edge loop | ![Shift-click before: vertical face loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1874a187aa3c58f81624f82571aa43aa317023e1/2281/shift-click-before.png) | ![Shift-click after: aligned horizontal face loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1874a187aa3c58f81624f82571aa43aa317023e1/2281/shift-click-after.png) |

Images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. No images or capture harness were committed to the PR branch. The existing Extend and Shift-click pins both failed under the temporary lookup mutation and passed after restoration.

## Not exercised
- No interactive mouse-driven GUI session ran. The captures above render the real shell and GPU viewport through the temporary test harness; existing state tests exercise `boundary_draft::extend` and `edge_pick::queue_edge_pick`.
- `boundary_draft::take_pick` still calls `extend_to_loop` (using `setup::active`, matching `view_pose`) rather than `extend_to_loop_in`, so it does not touch the function edited by open PR #2149.

## Overlaps
- `crates/ui/src/boundary_draft.rs`: PR #2149 edits `take_pick` and `refresh_preview` (different functions from `extend`; whichever merges second refreshes).
- `crates/app/src/operation/mod.rs`: PRs #2162, #2136, and #2035 touch different lines of this file (whichever merges second refreshes). PR #1738 lists `boundary_picks.rs` and `operation/mod.rs` against an older unmerged base, with no edits to `boundary_picks.rs` relative to `upstream/main`.

Effort: medium
Changelog: Boundary "Extend to loop" and Shift-click loop selection now read face normals in the setup's part-alignment frame.
Fixes #2216

title: feat(ui): debug info logs the frame rate on a change and docks as a tab
body:
What changed

- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/frame_rate.rs`: the frame-rate reading and its log rule. It reads the frame stamps that the shell already takes (frame cost rule, #2238). Work for each frame is O(1). It never requests a repaint.

title: fix(motion): enter each solid pass start by the asked entry in the pocket family
body:
## What changed

- `pass_link` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs`): a ladder that opts in (`Motion::with_solid_restart`) and whose user asked for a helix, ramp or arc entry enters a pass start in material (`plunge_law::into_solid`) by the new `entry_restart`. Before, a centre-cutting tool plunged straight down there, with no note.
- `entry_restart` (`descent_dive.rs`): the asked arm where the helix closes on the pass start or links to it at depth. Else a ramp along the pass. Else a plunge. Each stand-in has a note with the site, the level Z and the reason.
- `pocket_hsm.rs`: each piece of the area after the first keeps the `dive_room` start. The note says "entered at" (not "by an axial dive") when the entry is not Plunge. The pass link gives that start the helix. (The first head added a `choose_entry` seed. The review showed that it changed no result, so commit 1ba90baf2 removed it.)
- `pocket_emit.rs`: Pocket, rest 2D and Adaptive opt in. Contour, slot and trace do not opt in (follow-up #2269).
- Not changed: plunges into a cleared column or into air, operations with a Plunge entry, the rule for tools that are not centre-cutting, all verify checks, the post gate and all refusals.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2265-adaptive-entry-each-region.md`. Cause findings: issue comment on #2265.

## Readings and pinning tests

title: fix(ui): show a progress overlay over the viewport while a toolpath generates
body: #2257: while an operation generates its toolpath, the viewport shows no progress. The cause is that generation ran in the frame, on the UI thread. Thus no frame painted until the job ended. ## What changed - **Generation on a worker** (native window only). `GenerateOperation` already had a seam between the world reads and the pure work (M5.3 B). That seam is now public as `StagedGeneration`: - `StagedGeneration::new` reads the world on the UI thread. - `StagedGeneration::finish` runs the generator, the verification and the stamp on a worker thread. - The result lands through the same undoable `GenerateOperation` as before. The generators, the verify check and the post gate do not change. - **The overlay** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/gen_overlay.rs`) lies at the top centre of the viewport while a job runs. The navigation strip at the bottom and the view cube stay clear. It shows: - the label of the operation; - "(2 of 5)" when more generations wait in the queue; - the elapsed time and an activity bar (the generators report no fraction); - a `Cancel generation` button. - **Stale results are discarded.** The user can edit, undo or delete while the worker runs. A result lands only while its operation and its cached path are the same as at staging (`GenerateOperation::still_current`). If not, the status line says: `generation of X discarded: the operation changed while it generated - generate it again`. - **Cancel** drops the result and the queue. The old toolpath stays. A worker that runs finishes in the background, and its result is ignored. - **New and Open** drop a running generation. A result for the old document never lands in the new one. - **The viewport takes no press inside the overlay.** A click on Cancel is not also a viewport pick. - **Only the window turns it on** (`State::gen_jobs.background`). Tests, headless runs, scripts and MCP keep the synchronous path. `State::settle` waits for the worker. The browser has no threads: a failed spawn runs the job in place, as the import worker does. - **Repaint:** the shell asks for a repaint every 50 ms only while a job runs or waits (`view_pass::state_redraw_delay`). A frame with no job does no more work than before (#2238). - Decision record: `docs/decisions/2257-generate-progress-overlay.md`. ## What it looks like Rendered headless from the seeded shell at 1280x800 (a throwaway test, not in the branch). The images are below. - Before: while `Contour1` generates, the viewport shows nothing. - After: the overlay at the top centre, with the operation name, the elapsed time, the activity bar and `Cancel generation`. **Before** (the viewport while `Contour1` generates): **After** (the overlay at the top centre): ## Tests New pinning tests: - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/generate_progress.rs` (structural; the result comes through a channel that the test holds, so no frame races a real generator): - `the_overlay_names_the_running_operation_and_goes_when_it_lands`: the overlay text `Generating Contour1 - ...` is over the viewport, and the Cancel button is there while the job runs. The two go when the job lands. - `a_refusal_ends_the_overlay_and_keeps_its_message` - `cancel_ends_the_overlay_and_drops_the_result`: a click on Cancel ends the overlay. The status says that the generation is cancelled. No history entry is written. - `a_result_for_an_operation_edited_meanwhile_is_discarded`: the edit stays, and the old result writes nothing. - `background_generation_lands_the_same_toolpath`: a real worker run through `settle`. - `the_overlay_text_counts_a_batch` - `crates/app/tests/generate_staged.rs`: - `staged_then_finished_lands_what_the_one_shot_command_lands`: the same path either way. - `a_result_is_stale_after_an_edit_a_generation_or_a_delete` Gates on 08022981: - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (222 steps): green, with two exceptions. Neither comes from this change: - `app suites: wire_tool` does not compile on main. That is #2244 (`CuttingRow` gained `stepdown` and `stepover`). - `ui suites: lib`: three tests in `setup_picks_disarm` failed one time. They pass alone. The same suite on a clean `upstream/main` worktree fails 1 of 3 runs at `--test-threads=16` (`setup_picks_disarm`, `setup_mount_pages`). Thus the failures are timing failures on main. - `generate_progress` (6) and `generate_staged` (2): green after the last layout change. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --bins --test generate_staged -- -D warnings`: clean. `--all-targets` stops at `wire_tool` (#2244). - No snapshot PNG changed. ## Not exercised - No hand test in the real window on a long job. The structural tests drive the same `viewport_panel` code through the harness. - `RegenerateAll` (the batch fix of the stale operations) stays synchronous. Its rounds write the world between rounds, so it does not split at one seam. It shows no overlay. The overlay's "n of m" counts single generations that wait in the queue. - The browser build was not run. Its generation stays synchronous through the spawn fallback. Changelog: While a toolpath generates, a progress overlay over the viewport names the operation, counts the queued ones and offers Cancel; the window stays responsive (#2257) Effort: medium (the label of the issue). Not escalated. Fixes #2257 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(2d): hold crossing law on OffsetRings and Waterline pockets
body:
## What changed
- Updated `emit_pocket_passes` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_emit.rs` to hold `post_crossing_free` whenever `hold_crossings` is set or the strategy fits pass arcs (`Adaptive`, `OffsetRings`, or `Waterline`).
- Counted fitted arcs into `proof.arcs` in the `fit_arcs` branch so `ProofTally::note()` reports accurate totals when a crossing arc returns to chords.
- Added unit pin `offset_rings_across_one_micron_vertex_step_post_crossing_free` and integration suite `crates/app/tests/adaptive_fig8_crossing.rs`.
- Recorded the design decision in `docs/decisions/2240-adaptive-fig8-crossing.md`.

## Cause
- On `fig8.step` (tight stock or stock excluding the top face), 2D Adaptive refuses the HSM planner and falls back to `PocketStrategy::OffsetRings`.
- Clipper2 integer quantization (`1e-6 mm` grid) on STEP-faceted circles creates micron-scale vertex steps that split `fit_arcs` across `sag_bound` into `[Arc, 1 um Line, Arc]`.
- Because `ARC_FIT_TOL` (`0.01 mm`) exceeds the `1 um` line, adjacent arc chord brackets cross in XY at shared depth and block posting.
- `emit_pocket_passes` previously checked `post_crossing_free` only for `Adaptive` and `hold_crossings` (`rest2d`), leaving `OffsetRings` and `Waterline` pockets unguarded.

## Tests
- Pin `offset_rings_across_one_micron_vertex_step_post_crossing_free` (`camcraft-motion`): failed on unguarded `upstream/main` logic (`[[5, 7], [15, 17]]`), passed after restoring the fix.
- Pins `adaptive2d_on_fig8_model_in_tight_stock_has_no_crossings_and_posts` and `adaptive2d_on_fig8_stock_excluding_top_face_has_no_crossings_and_posts` (`camcraft-app --test adaptive_fig8_crossing`): failed on unguarded `upstream/main` logic (`[[69, 71], [197, 199], [1003, 1005], [1131, 1133]]` and `[[69, 71], [197, 199], [1338, 1340], [1466, 1468]]`), passed after restoring the fix (`0` crossings, `0` warnings, clean simulation and post).
- Mutation check: reverted `hold_fitted` and `proof.arcs` in `pocket_emit.rs` to `upstream/main`, confirmed both pin targets failed (`0` passed), restored the fix, and confirmed both passed.
- Extra `camcraft-motion` integration suites (`adaptive_hsm`, `adaptive_orbit_seam`, `corner_blend_arc`, `machining2d`, `optimal_load`, `rest2d`): passed (`0` failed; `5` ignored heavy tests in `adaptive_hsm`).
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed (`wall 11.6 min, 2 step(s), 0 failed`).
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test adaptive_fig8_crossing -- -D warnings` passed.

## Goldens moved
- None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` failed to compile untouched pre-existing `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs` on branch base `e3f7d122b` (fixed later on `upstream/main` in `#2263`).
- Full `gate batch` and `gate release` suites did not run in this worker; only `gate quick` and the six listed `camcraft-motion` 2D suites ran.

## Overlaps
- None among open PRs (`pocket_emit.rs` and `adaptive_fig8_crossing.rs` have no open PR overlaps).

Changelog: Fix 2D Adaptive feed crossings on fig8 by enforcing the crossing law on OffsetRings and Waterline passes.

Fixes #2240

## Latest review fix: release heavy lane

Both fig8 tests now have ignore reasons that name the release heavy lane:

- `adaptive2d_on_fig8_model_in_tight_stock_has_no_crossings_and_posts`
- `adaptive2d_on_fig8_stock_excluding_top_face_has_no_crossings_and_posts`

Both tests keep their crossing, verification, and post assertions. The fast motion regression stays active.

- Release run: `cargo test --release -p camcraft-app --test adaptive_fig8_crossing -- --ignored --test-threads=1`: 2 passed, 0 failed in 36.74 seconds (190.51 seconds with the build).
- Lane mutation check: Removing both ignore attributes made the ignored-inventory check fail with 0 tests. Restoring them passed with 2 tests. The default debug run reported 0 passed and 2 ignored.
- Fast motion regression: `offset_rings_across_one_micron_vertex_step_post_crossing_free` passed (1 passed, 0 ignored).
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED after 6.7 minutes. The batch debug build failed at unchanged `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs:106–107`. Error E0308 requires `Option` for `material`. Error E0063 reports missing `stepdown` and `stepover` fields.
- Clippy, all targets with warnings denied: `camcraft-cl` and `camcraft-motion` passed for all targets with warnings denied. The app library and `adaptive_fig8_crossing` target also passed with warnings denied. The app all-targets check failed at the unchanged `wire_tool.rs` fixture with the same gate errors.

title: fix(mcp): batch AI undo, add get_selection, and enforce live confirmation gate
body:
## Before/after screenshots

Real 1280×720 egui shell renders with offline `ScriptedTransport`. Images live only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch at `775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1`.

| Behavior | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One Ctrl+Z after a three-command AI turn | ![Stock and tool remain after undo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1/2260/before-one-ctrl-z.png) | ![All three turn edits removed after undo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1/2260/after-one-ctrl-z.png) |
| Native-mode machine edit | ![Machine loads without confirmation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1/2260/before-machine-confirmation.png) | ![Machine edit waits for Allow or Deny](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/775c2b7ce0ff9d017a6161fd6784fe901bfae2a1/2260/after-machine-confirmation.png) |

The before renders reproduce the prior behavior with temporary reversions: disable history-group folding for undo; restore the former Native confirmation allowlist and bypass the newly added live gate for `load_machine` for machine loading. The after renders use the current PR behavior. All capture edits were restored; no screenshots or capture code were added to this PR branch.

Existing pins were mutation-checked again: `one_ctrl_z_reverts_multi_call_ai_chat_turn` and `machine_and_limit_edits_require_confirmation_and_unapproved_live_dispatch_blocks` both failed with their behavior reverted and passed after restoration.

## What changed
- Added `BatchCommand` and stackable `History::begin_group` / `commit_group` / `cancel_group` in `crates/app/src/commands/batch.rs` and `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs`.
- Wired `State::submit_ai_prompt`, `State::run`, `AiChatState::poll`, and `ChatTurn::finish` so a contiguous multi-call AI turn commits as one `BatchCommand` undo step (`Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Y`).
- Added the read-only `get_selection` MCP tool (`crates/app/src/mcp/selection.rs`) and `SelectionContext` snapshot (`State::selection_context`) so live sessions report selected entities, active setup, selected/active operation, viewport `pick_mode`, and `geometry_picks` without breaking `ui -> app` layering.
- Added `LiveGate`, `GateKind`, `ApprovedCall`, `requires_approval`, `LiveOptions`, and `answer_live_with` in `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs`; `answer_live` now fails closed via `&LiveOptions::default()`.
- Updated `AiChatState`, `transport::requires_confirmation`, `worker`, and `mcp_host::pump` to share `requires_approval` and `is_read_only_tool`, bind `Allow` clicks to one `ApprovedCall`, and never auto-approve `post`, `load_machine`, or `edit_machine`.
- Updated `undo_turn_reverts_multi_tool_turn_changes_in_one_click_and_guards_later_edits` (`#2094`) from `pre_depth + 3` to `pre_depth + 1` to reflect the collapsed `BatchCommand` entry.
- Recorded design decisions in `docs/decisions/1942-ai-chat-safety.md`.

## Cause
Before this fix, AI chat turns pushed one `History` entry per tool call (requiring multiple `Ctrl+Z` presses), `get_selection` did not exist for AI inspection of viewport picks, `FallbackMode::Native` skipped confirmation for machine and limit tools, and `answer_live` lacked a server-side permission gate.

## Tests
Pinning tests (all red on unchanged `upstream/main` `e808c9629`, green after fix):
- `camcraft-app --test batch_undo`: `begin_and_commit_group_folds_multi_command_turn_into_one_undo_step`, `empty_and_nested_groups_and_direct_batch_command_behave_cleanly`, `cancel_group_keeps_existing_commands_separate` (3 passed, 0 failed).
- `camcraft-app --test mcp_live`: `get_selection_returns_selected_entities_and_empty_picks_headless`, `live_permission_gate_blocks_unapproved_post_file_writes_paths_and_machine_limits`, `get_selection_reads_live_ui_selection_context_and_prompt_json_treats_it_read_only`, `live_gate_allows_explicitly_approved_calls_and_never_auto_approves_post_or_machine_edits` (14 passed, 0 failed in `mcp_live`; `mcp`: 22 passed; `mcp_provider`: 9 passed).

title: perf(ui): group welded faces once per feature set for the pick chips
body:
Stacked on #2255. The base is `issue/2246-area-preview-fill`. Retarget this PR to `main` before #2255 merges.

- `State::geo_chips` (welded-face chip label) and `pick::face_origin` read the memo. `face_origin` is used by the chips and by `pick::align_321`.
- `face_origin` finds the strips of a patch with a binary search in the sorted `Patch::faces`. Before, it did a linear `contains` for each face of the model.

The answers are the same as a fresh grouping. No change to commands, picks, the WCS result, cut geometry or posted G-code.

title: fix(ui): cache pick highlight geometry and batch stroke draws
body:
## What changed

- Added thread-local weak lookup indexes (`resolve_chain_arc`, `patches_arc`, `patch_rings_arc`) in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature/index.rs`.
- Removed per-triangle heap allocations in `digest_of` and hoisted lattice construction in `patches` and `patch_rings` inside `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs`.
- Added `SHARED_FEATURES_CACHE` (`Weak<[Triangle]>`, cap 32) in `crates/app/src/model/geometry.rs` so repeated `features_of` reads skip `digest_of`.
- Added non-cloning `toolpath_nonempty` and `toolpath_warning_count` in `crates/app/src/model.rs`, used them in `operation::stamp::status_of` and `browser_tree::op_row`, and added `History::revision_token` in `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs`.
- Switched `Arc<Features>` lookups in `crates/app/src/operation/{selection.rs, stitch.rs}`, `crates/app/src/pick/{face.rs, feature_sel.rs}`, and `crates/ui/src/{edge_pick.rs, interact.rs, state.rs}` to `*_arc` helpers.
- Added `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight.rs` (`HighlightCache`) to resolve selected, hovered, and row-hovered outlines once per state change.
- Added `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight_mesh.rs` to tessellate each highlight layer into one cached `egui::Shape::Mesh` in `pick_ink::paint` and `shell::viewport_panel`.
- Added `crates/ui/src/frame_cache.rs` and `crates/ui/src/panel_cache.rs` on `State` to cache world vertices, cutting regions and outlines, toolpath overlay lines, non-transient `world::Scene` plus digest, Geometry chips, 3-2-1 datum checks, selection account, unresolved notes, operation status banners, and browser operation rows.
- Review fix (`b654e0502`): `WorldVertsEntry` in `crates/ui/src/frame_cache.rs` keeps a `Weak<[Triangle]>` of the source facets, not a raw address. A released source cannot match, and its address cannot be reused while the entry holds the `Weak`. Dead entries are pruned on each lookup.
- Added architecture decision record in `docs/decisions/2201-highlighter-frame-perf.md`.

## Cause

- On models with many chains or facets, `features_of` re-hashed triangle buffers and `resolve_chain` re-walked and split chains repeatedly during frame, highlight, and panel queries.
- `pick_ink::paint` and `shell::viewport_panel` emitted two individual `Shape::LineSegment` shapes per projected segment per frame.
- `world::collect`, `toolpath_lines`, `stamp::status_of`, `browser_tree::op_row`, `op_page`, and `geo_page` rebuilt and cloned vertices, outlines, warnings, and toolpaths on every frame even when inputs stayed unchanged.

## Screenshots

Real `1280x720` shell and `View3D` renders. Before is `1f15f98e7` (the PR base). After is `b654e0502`. The images are only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.

| Welded face | ![Before welded face](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/3441230386b638c8bfd4478b8cb22b908ff25aad/2256/before-welded-face.png) | ![After welded face](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/3441230386b638c8bfd4478b8cb22b908ff25aad/2256/after-welded-face.png) |

## Tests

- UI pinning tests in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/highlight_perf.rs` (`4 passed; 0 failed` in `camcraft-ui`):
  - `three_selected_edge_pieces_draw_as_a_single_batched_highlight` (red on unchanged code)
  - `selected_highlight_builds_once_at_selection_and_zero_times_across_orbit_idle_and_hover` (red on unchanged code)

  - `dense_45k_model_with_multiple_ops_and_many_limit_findings_stays_stable_across_frames` (red on unchanged code)
- Vertex cache pins in `crates/ui/src/frame_cache_tests.rs` (review fix):
  - `frame_cache::tests::world_verts_cached_does_not_reuse_stale_entry_after_source_release`

  - `resolve_chain_arc_matches_uncached_for_chains_runs_singletons_and_missing`
