title: feat(ui,app): wire browser app tracing, dropped model bytes, and inline CpuEye fallback
body:
## What changed

- Added `camcraft_app::logging::dispatch(writer, browser)` using `.without_time().with_ansi(false)` for browser builds, and called `camcraft_app::logging::init()` inside `camcraft_start` (`crates/app/src/logging.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs`).
- Updated `file_drop::take_drop` with `check_drop_bytes` and `deliver_model_bytes` to load bare-name dropped model bytes through `file_pick::deliver` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/file_drop.rs`).
- Refactored `CpuEye` into `Mode::Threaded` and `Mode::Inline(Box<Inline>)` sharing `march_job`, falling back to `CpuEye::inline()` on `wasm32` or `ErrorKind::Unsupported` (`crates/ui/src/trace/cpu_eye.rs`).
- Added `StockEye::cpu_pending` and requested frame repaints in `WebShell::ui` while inline marching is pending (`crates/ui/src/trace/eye.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs`).
- Recorded the design choices in `docs/decisions/31-wasm-browser-runtime.md`.

## Cause

- `camcraft_start` did not initialize `camcraft_app::logging`, and default `tracing_subscriber::fmt` emits ANSI escapes and calls `SystemTime::now()`, which panics on `wasm32`.
- `file_drop::take_drop` routed bare-name browser drops into `classify`, which refused them because `path.is_file()` is false in browser builds.
- `CpuEye::spawn` failed without OS threads, and `WebShell::ui` did not poll pending CPU work for repaints.

## Tests

- Pins (red before fix, green after fix):
  - `crates/app/tests/logging.rs::browser_subscriber_omits_timestamps_and_ansi_escapes` (red before fix: E0425 compile error; green after fix)
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/file_drop.rs`: `a_bare_name_dropped_mesh_with_bytes_imports_and_undoes`, `a_bare_name_drop_with_bad_extension_or_read_error_is_refused_by_name` (red before fix: `drop refused: cube.stl is not a readable file`; green after fix)
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/browser_files.rs::browser_shell_initializes_app_logging_and_repaints_pending_cpu_eye` (red before fix: assertion failed; green after fix)
  - `crates/ui/src/trace/cpu_eye.rs::tests::inline_cpu_eye_marches_without_spawning_a_thread` (red before fix: E0599 compile error; green after fix)
- Mutations (file reverted to `upstream/main` -> red, restored -> green):
  - `crates/app/src/logging.rs`: red (compile error) / green
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs`: red / green
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/file_drop.rs`: red / green
  - `crates/ui/src/trace/cpu_eye.rs`: red (compile error) / green
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, after final edit):
  - `camcraft-app` lib: `352 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored` (`a_smooth_face_needing_more_than_the_old_cap_is_divided_not_tripped`, heavy lane)
  - `camcraft-app` `logging`: `5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored`
  - `camcraft-ui` lib: `952 passed; 0 failed; 6 ignored` (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `review_1710_wcs_page_and_viewport_evidence`, `tool_editor_snapshot`, `a_full_length_jump_on_the_worker_costs_no_more_than_the_direct_seek`, `traced_playback_cost_per_frame_and_per_jump`)
  - `camcraft-ui` integration suites: `boundary` (`3 passed`), `boundary_picks` (`6 passed`), `sinker_setup` (`2 passed`), `tap_hand` (`3 passed`), `theme_files` (`15 passed`), `trace_composite` (`4 passed`), `trace_parity` (`5 passed`), `waterjet_tool` (`1 passed`); `0 failed; 0 ignored`
- Clippy (`cargo xtask gate batch --only clippy`, `-D warnings` across all 8 workspace crates `--all-targets`): passed in 3s (`0 failed`).

## Browser evidence (review follow-up)

The before/after pairs show browser dropped-file import and CPU stock preview. The PR source and head remain unchanged at `28d3295ba3f2e4e3e24c5600abb5b77059d5f1af`. These are actual browser captures, not native snapshots.

Build: debug `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with `web/build-app-wasm.sh`, Rust 1.99.1, Clang 21, WASI SDK 34 sysroot and wasm-bindgen 0.2.129. Both browsers ran on Linux at 1440 × 1000, device scale 1.

The before build is a temporary source copy of this head with `crates/ui/src/egui_app/file_drop.rs`, `crates/ui/src/trace/cpu_eye.rs` and `crates/ui/src/trace/eye.rs` taken from its parent `a529c455352d8c2d228e3dd83d0e5d42a91ea9b0`, and the pending-CPU repaint clause removed from `shell_web.rs`. It retains this PR's browser logging initialization and formatter so startup succeeds and the import and CPU regressions can be isolated. The after build uses the unchanged PR head.

Browser import: Chromium 159.0.8154.6, headless ANGLE SwiftShader, with WebGPU disabled so the app uses WebGL2. Both captures drop the same in-memory `browser-block.stl` file (a 30 × 20 × 10 mm cuboid) onto the canvas.

| Before: bare-name browser drop refused | After: model imported from browser bytes |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: browser drop refused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eb739294174052ce25c2a274dc3f5bbf59c4b984/2239/import-before.png) | ![After: browser model imported](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eb739294174052ce25c2a274dc3f5bbf59c4b984/2239/import-after.png) |

CPU stock preview: Firefox 159.0, headless WebGPU with Mesa Vulkan llvmpipe (Mesa 26.0.8). WebGPU preferences were `dom.webgpu.enabled=true`, `gfx.webgpu.force-enabled=true` and `dom.webgpu.allow-software-adapter=true`; the process used `MOZ_DISABLE_CONTENT_SANDBOX=1` and `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.json`. Both captures open the same generated project (closed cuboid model, 40 × 40 × 10 mm box stock, Ø6 end mill and one 2D Contour), regenerate the stale operation, then click Deviate.

To exercise the CPU fallback on this working WebGPU adapter, both stock runs use the same browser-side hook: `GPUDevice.prototype.createShaderModule` replaces only shader descriptors whose label is `trace` with the invalid WGSL string `controlled_trace_validation_refusal`. The app's existing validation error scope reports that the compute kernel was refused and that the CPU march stands in. The composite pipeline is untouched. This hook changes no production source and is disclosed because these captures demonstrate controlled fallback, not a naturally failing adapter.

| Before: CPU worker cannot start in the browser | After: inline CPU preview renders |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: CPU stock preview refused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eb739294174052ce25c2a274dc3f5bbf59c4b984/2239/stock-before.png) | ![After: inline CPU stock preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eb739294174052ce25c2a274dc3f5bbf59c4b984/2239/stock-after.png) |

The before stock capture retains the transparent stock sheet; its browser console reports `cpu eye: the worker would not start: operation not supported on this platform`. The after stock capture shows the coarse CPU preview and the Deviate result: REST 729 cells, 512.58 mm³, worst 5.00 mm. The images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. No screenshots, logs or review evidence were committed to the PR branch. This follow-up changes only the PR body and adds no code or tests requiring a new mutation check. Existing pins are `a_bare_name_dropped_mesh_with_bytes_imports_and_undoes`, `inline_cpu_eye_marches_without_spawning_a_thread` and `browser_shell_initializes_app_logging_and_repaints_pending_cpu_eye`; the original code mutation results remain listed above.

## Goldens moved

- `none` (`git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Live browser import and a controlled CPU stock-preview fallback were exercised as documented above. A natural device rejection of the trace kernel was not available on the working WebGPU adapter, so that fallback evidence uses the disclosed browser-side validation fault injection.
- Remaining `#31` work deferred to separate PRs: inline `PlayWorker` fallback in `stock_play_worker.rs` (overlapped by `#2192`), `shell.rs` viewport split (overlapped by `#2110` and `#1330`), and removing `#![cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", allow(dead_code))]` in `crates/ui/src/lib.rs`.

## Overlaps

- PR `#2150` touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/file_drop.rs` in `MESH_EXTENSIONS`, `classify`, and its tests; this PR touches `take_drop` and adds `check_drop_bytes` and `deliver_model_bytes` (different functions; whichever merges second refreshes).

Changelog: Browser builds now route app tracing to the console without panicking, load dropped model files from bytes, and fall back to inline CPU stock preview when threads cannot spawn.

Effort: high

Refs #31

title: fix(tools): a refused tool names itself and the rule it breaks
body:
#1186: the project loader refused a tool with bad numbers. The message was `tool parameters are not usable: ToolDto { ... }`, with the full structure. The refusal was correct, but it did not name the tool or the field. `AddTool` and `ChangeTool` printed a similar dump. The library import and the library reader gave a general message.

The branch has upstream main at a529c455, merged in.

## What changed

- **`Tool::why_not_sane() -> Option<String>`** (new file `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs`). It gives the first rule that a tool breaks, in plain words. Examples:
  - `turning surface speed 0 m/min is outside 0..2000 m/min (it must be over 0)`
  - `corner radius 100 mm is more than half the 6 mm diameter`
  - `a drill's tip angle 50 degrees must be over 60`
  - `a sinker electrode turns no spindle: its spindle speed must be 0, not 1000 rpm`
  - `TurningData::why_not_sane` gives the same for the turning limits.
- **One source of truth.** `Tool::is_sane` and `TurningData::is_sane` are now `why_not_sane().is_none()`. Thus the message and the verdict cannot be different. The rules moved out of `tools.rs` in the same order, with the same limits.
- **The rules that main added are included.** Main added these after the branch started:
  - the `pitch_min` field;
  - the waterjet, electrode and thread-mill kinds and their rules;
  - the catalog and cutting-row refusals.
  - Each of these rules has its own message now.
- **Four refusals now read `tool '<name>': <rule>`:**
  - the project loader (`project/validate.rs`), which is the case in the issue;
  - `AddTool` and `ChangeTool` (`commands/tool.rs`);
  - the tool-library import (`commands/tool_import.rs`);
  - the library reader (`tool_library.rs`).
  - The MCP tools `add_tool` and `edit_tool` use the same commands. Thus an agent also gets the named rule.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1186-tool-refusal-names.md`.

## Tests

New pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/project_tool_refusal.rs` opens a saved file with one bad field through the real loader (`project::open`).
  - `a_bad_turning_field_is_refused_by_tool_and_field`: surface speed 0, a negative feed per rev, and a max rpm below the rpm of the tool.
  - `a_bad_milling_field_is_refused_by_tool_and_field`: a corner radius more than half the diameter, and feed 0.
  - The two tests also make sure that the message has no `ToolDto` dump.
- `tools::tool_sanity::tests`:
  - `a_turning_field_is_named`, `a_milling_field_is_named` and `the_newer_kinds_are_named`.
  - `the_named_law_gives_the_old_verdict_everywhere` keeps the `is_sane` body of main as an oracle. It also keeps the `TurningData::is_sane` body.
  - The test examines each catalog tool as each of the 17 kinds. It sets each of the 14 numeric fields to 13 edge values: 0, negative, the 60 and 180 degree limits, more than 500, NaN and infinity. It also examines flute counts, orientation codes and turning data.
  - The new law gives the same verdict in all cases. Thus no tool changes from accepted to refused, or from refused to accepted.

Changed test: `tool_cutter_params::a_reshape_is_refused_by_name_against_the_new_numbers` looked for the old text "finite and positive". It now looks for `tool '<name>': diameter -1 mm is outside`.

Gates on dbf7799e:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green.
  - The tools step ran the lib tests and `waterjet`.
  - The app step ran the lib tests and 44 suites. These include all `tool_*` suites, `project_tool_refusal`, `project_roundtrip`, `thread_mill`, `waterjet_machine`, `plasma_profile`, `mcp` and `commands_undo`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised

- The UI shows these refusals in the status line, as before. No UI test reads their text. A search of `crates/ui` finds none of the old messages.
- A missing or unknown field is a serde parse error. It occurs before this law runs. The serde message already names the field, and it does not change.

Changelog: A tool refused for unusable numbers (project load, add or edit tool, library import) now names the tool and the rule it breaks, e.g. "tool 'T1': turning surface speed 0 m/min is outside 0..2000 m/min", instead of printing the whole definition (#1186)

Effort: low (the label of the issue). Not escalated.

Fixes #1186

title: feat(sim): calculate the playback stock removal before playback
body:
## What changed

The traced playback worker now cuts the whole program one time when the transport starts. It keeps keyframes of the cut stock at a fixed stride. After that, a jump forward or back restores the keyframe at or before the playhead and cuts at most one stride. The program is not cut again during playback.

- `crates/sim/src/play_keys.rs`: `Precalc` state and the checkpoint store, with byte accounting and thinning shared by precalculation and live seeks after cancellation (512 MiB default budget, at most 1024 keyframes, at least 64 moves apart initially).
- `crates/sim/src/play_precalc.rs`: begin/step orchestration, checkpoint policy and the calculation loop through the `Playback` seam. `Keyframes::restores` is the one seek law for `FieldPlay::seek` and the worker.
- `crates/sim/src/play_precalc_mailbox.rs`: progress and cancellation state, with caller-provided stop and elapsed-time bindings.
- `crates/app/src/stock_play_precalc.rs`, `stock_play_worker_precalc.rs`: thin adapters for the existing `FieldPlay` and `PlayWorker` APIs. App retains document gathering, thread lifetime, wakeups, clock binding and frame publication. It re-exports the sim API where needed.
- `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs`, `stock_play_worker.rs`: a seek restores a keyframe that is more than one stride ahead, not only one behind. A `moves_cut` counter measures the replay law.
- `crates/ui/src/actions.rs`: the transport starts the worker with the calculation.
- `crates/ui/src/play_precalc.rs` (new), `egui_app/shell.rs`: a line under the transport shows the progress and a Cancel button. A stopped calculation shows "incomplete" with the reason.
- `docs/decisions/2181-sim-precalc.md`: the design and the dropped options.

The stamp is `doc_version`. Each command retires the worker and frees its keyframes (an operation delete included). The keyframes are display only. The Deviate verdict and the post gate do not read them.

## Readings

Release, dense face (100 mm block, stepover 0.5, stepdown 0.5, `DEFAULT_TEXELS`), `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face`:

- 4268 moves, 68 keyframes, stride 64
- keyframe memory 444940288 bytes (424 MiB, under the 512 MiB budget)
- calculation time 23.9 s

During the calculation the sheet stands and the line shows the progress. Follow-up #2193 serves frames during the calculation. Follow-up #2194 lowers the keyframe memory.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs`:
- `the_precalculated_stock_is_the_live_cut_at_every_position` (bit-identical cut layer at each move, forward and back jumps mixed)
- `a_jump_after_the_calculation_cuts_at_most_one_stride` (no new full calculation)
- `the_keyframes_stay_within_the_memory_budget`
- `a_stopped_calculation_leaves_exact_keyframes_and_cuts_the_rest_live`
- `the_worker_calculates_first_then_replays_and_the_post_gate_is_unchanged` (`posting::verification_gate` is equal before and after)
- `a_cancelled_calculation_is_incomplete_by_name_and_playback_goes_on`
- `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` (ignored, heavy lane, the reading above)

`crates/sim/tests/play_precalc.rs` (#2192 review, finding 4):
- `domain_calculation_resets_cuts_and_reports_the_bounded_store`
- `domain_mailbox_cancel_preserves_partial_checkpoints_and_names_the_end`
- `domain_mailbox_reports_progress_and_uses_the_owners_stop_and_clock`
- `a_seek_restores_behind_or_more_than_a_stride_ahead`

`crates/ui/src/play_precalc_tests.rs`:
- `the_readout_says_progress_and_incomplete_and_nothing_when_done`
- `an_edit_of_the_operation_retires_the_stored_calculation`

## Gate

Fix round at head 5d929ae (finding 4 again; the local commit 738492b of the earlier round was never pushed, so this round makes the move again on the pushed branch):

- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --test play_precalc --test play_keys`: 4 + 4 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test stock_play --test stock_play_precalc --test stock_play_partial --test stock_sim_document`: 7, 7 (1 ignored, the heavy reading), 3, 9 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib precalc`: 6 pass (the transport row and readout tests). No ui file changed in this round.
- Clippy with `-D warnings`: sim all targets; app lib and the four suites above; ui lib and tests.
- Mutation: with the keyframe offer removed from `play_precalc::step`, two of the new sim pins fail. The restored source passes.
- Not run: the quick tier (over one hour on sim branches), the full app and ui suites, the heavy lanes.

## Screenshots

Headless render of the real shell (test harness, 1280x720), captured in the earlier fix round and preserved from image commit `a94079e073ac7e38f14569eca085dec7a903e17a`. The before image shows the transport before precalculation. The after images show the reviewed transport change. These PNGs are hosted only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

Before: the transport row has no precalculation line.

![before](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-2192/before-transport.png>)

After, while the calculation runs: the progress text and the Cancel button.

![after running](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-2192/after-running.png>)

After, when Cancel stopped the calculation: the "incomplete" text with the reason. There is no Cancel button.

![after incomplete](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-2192/after-incomplete.png>)

## Not exercised

- The windowed app was not started. The screenshots come from the headless test harness render of the real shell.
- The reading uses one large fixture only.

## Overlap

#2182 changes other hunks of `crates/ui/src/actions.rs` (status strings). The two PRs do not stack.

Changelog: Simulation playback calculates the stock removal one time before it plays, then replays it, so a jump on the timeline does not lag. A line under the transport shows the progress and can cancel the calculation.

Effort: high (issue label effort:max; an Opus worker of the high tier works it by the maintainer's order; no escalation)

Fixes #2181

title: feat(fixtures): turn a fixture by quarter turns or a typed angle
body:
## What changed

- New undoable command `TurnFixture` (`crates/app/src/commands/fixture_turn.rs`). It turns one fixture about world X, Y or Z through the fixture origin. The write is a `MoveFixture`, so plate riders turn with the fixture.
- Quarter turns write exact quaternion components (`settle_rot`). A turn that changes nothing (0 or 360 degrees) is refused. This obeys #2177.
- A part or the stock that touched the fixture before the turn stays in position. The warning names each one (`fixture_clash::held_by`).
- The turn does not make toolpaths stale. The post gate reads the turned fixture live. A turn into the tool path blocks the post with "strikes a fixture".
- Fixtures page place draft: "Place yaw" is replaced by "Tilt about X (roll)", "Tilt about Y (pitch)" and "Turn about Z (yaw)". Six buttons "Turn X+" .. "Turn Z-" apply a quarter turn immediately. The row text shows roll and pitch when the fixture is not upright.
- New MCP tool `turn_fixture` (`crates/app/src/mcp/fixture_turn_tools.rs`), with a row in the `camcraft-mcp` skill.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2174-fixture-turns.md`.

Process change: yes (one row added to `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/fixture_turn.rs`: `a_quarter_turn_about_each_axis_is_exact_and_undo_and_redo_restore_it`, `a_typed_angle_turns_by_it_and_undo_and_redo_restore_it`, `four_quarter_turns_are_the_exact_start_and_a_zero_turn_is_refused`, `a_fixture_turned_into_the_tools_path_blocks_the_post_without_a_regenerate`, `a_turned_fixture_names_the_stock_it_held_and_a_free_one_names_nothing`.

title: feat(ui): drag rings in Rotate mode turn the selected part
body:
Stacked on #1330. This branch starts from the head of #1330 (`58df4b729`, fork branch `mkinney:issue/1198-drag-to-move`) with `origin/main` merged in. Until #1330 merges, the diff shows the commits of #1330 too. The new work is commit `043b7e0a9`.

## What changed
- The viewport bar has a new Rotate button after Move. Move and Rotate are mutually exclusive. A toggle cancels the live drag of the other mode.
- With Rotate on, the one selected part shows three rings round its bounding-box centre. Each ring is square to one shown axis. The ring radius is a constant 60 px on the screen. A press within 6 px of a ring grabs the nearest ring.
- The drag angle is the point where the cursor ray meets the ring plane, measured about the centre. The angle is unwrapped, so a drag can go past 180 degrees. During the drag the part preview turns and the bar shows `Turn about Z: +35.0°`. The world does not change during the drag.
- The release queues one `CommandKind::TurnModelBy { name, axis, angle_rad }`. The drain runs the existing `MoveModel`, so the turn is one undo step. The generated operations go stale and the stock follows the part, as for a typed turn.
- An aligned setup turns the part about the axis that the user sees (the turn goes back through the setup alignment).
- Escape cancels the turn with no history step. A turn that ends at its start angle queues nothing and writes no rotation noise (#2177).
- A bad axis, a non-finite angle or a missing part is refused by name on the status line.
- New files: `crates/ui/src/turn_drag.rs` (the drag law), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/turn_handles.rs` (the paint), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewport_bar_tests.rs` (the bar tests moved out to keep `viewport_bar.rs` near 400 lines).
- No new app command, so no new MCP tool. MCP `move_model` already sets the rotation.

## How the stale path is pinned
`body_turn::a_ring_drag_is_one_undoable_turn_that_stales_the_path_and_carries_the_stock` drags the Z ring on the seeded document. Before the drag, `camcraft_app::posting::program_ops` returns `Ok`. After the release, it returns an `Err` that contains "regenerate", so the post refuses. One undo makes the history clean again and `program_ops` returns `Ok` again. The same test checks that the stock box still holds the turned part. The app-level pin `crates/app/tests/commands_undo.rs::a_moved_part_marks_generated_ops_stale_and_undo_clears_it` already covers a pure rotation in the stale stamp.

## Pinning tests
- `egui_app::tests::body_turn::*` (5 tests): rings only in Rotate mode at a constant size; one undoable turn that makes the path stale and carries the stock; Escape cancels; a zero turn adds nothing; empty space still orbits.
- `turn_drag_tests::*` (6 tests): the angle under the cursor, a drag past half a turn, no command for a press off the rings or a turn in place, the centre stays in place, a turned setup, refusals by name.
- `egui_app::viewport_bar::tests::move_and_rotate_modes_never_share_the_part`.

## Readings
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`) on head `043b7e0a9`: ui lib 954 passed, 1 failed; boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, sinker_setup, tap_hand, theme_files, waterjet_tool all green. The one failure is `stock_fit_controls_follow_the_selected_shape`, which also fails on main (#2170, fix PR #2171).
- Clippy `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised
- No hand test in the live window. The screenshots come from the kittest harness render of the shipping shell with the GPU viewport, at 1280x720.
- No angle snapping (not asked for; see `docs/decisions/2047-drag-to-rotate.md`).
- `shell.rs` was already longer than 400 lines before this change; this PR adds 11 lines to it.

## Screenshots
Before (Move mode of #1330 on this branch: the move balls, no rings):
![before move](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/c75bf71a4a9cb55f12442cdc2b6b5b8775178e51/pr-2047/before-move.png?raw=true)
After (Rotate mode, a Z-ring drag of +35 degrees in progress):
![after rotate](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/c75bf71a4a9cb55f12442cdc2b6b5b8775178e51/pr-2047/after-rotate.png?raw=true)

title: fix(fixtures): locate the stock on an existing vise
body:
## What changed

The locate took mates on the part only. Thus a user could not seat the stock on a vise that was already placed. The fixture collision checks and the carried-workholding check then read a stock place that nobody set.

- `fixture_locate`: `LocateSpec` has a new field `body` (`LocateBody::Part` is the default, `LocateBody::Stock` is new). `stock_of` finds the stock of the fixture's setup. With the stock held, the mates are on the stock, in the stock's own pose.
- `LocatePart`: with the stock held, the part moves and the stock follows it (stock-follow law). The part keeps its place in the blank. The locate is one undo step.
- Refusals by name: a stock locate with no part, a setup with no stock, a mate on the wrong body. A square stock re-fits round a turned part with the allowance of each setup side. If that re-fit leaves the stock faces off the mates, `stock_lands` refuses the locate ("would not land on the mates").
- Review fix (head `32102879d`): `stock_lands` (now in `crates/app/src/fixture_locate_land.rs`) judges each picked stock face, not only the box of the stock. The face is placed where the mates put it. The followed stock must have facets that face the same way (`NORMAL_TOL` = 1e-4 on 1 - cos of the angle, about 0.8 degree) and lie on that plane (`LEN_TOL_MM` = 1e-4 mm). These facets must cover the face area (`FACE_AREA_REL_TOL` = 0.1 %) and each facet centre of the face. A picked stock vertex must be a corner of the followed stock. A failure is refused in `LocatePart::new`. The message names the stock face and the fixture face: "mate N: <stock face> of the stock '<stock>' would stand across the plane of, not flat on, <fixture face> of '<fixture>' - ... locate it without a turn, or locate the part".
- MCP: `locate_part` takes `"body": "stock"` (the default is `"part"`). `list_features` lists the faces of a stock.
- UI: the locate form shows "Place by: Stock faces / Part faces". It holds the stock by default when the fixture's setup has a stock. While the stock is held, the picks pass over the parts inside the stock, so a stock face round a part can be picked.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2173-locate-stock-on-vise.md`.

## Effect on checks and posted output

No change for existing projects and scripts: the API and MCP default stay `Part`. The new path moves the part and its stock as a part locate does. The existing locate tests pass unchanged.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/fixture_locate_stock_body.rs`:
  - `the_stock_locates_on_an_existing_vise_and_undo_puts_it_back`
  - `the_fixture_collision_check_reads_the_located_stock` (`fixture_clash::after_fixture_move` reads the located stock)
  - `a_stock_that_would_miss_its_mates_is_refused_by_name`
  - `the_part_stays_the_default_body`
  - `mcp_locate_part_seats_the_stock_by_its_feature_ids`
- `crates/app/tests/fixture_locate_stock_cylinder.rs` (review fix):
  - `a_cylinder_cap_mated_across_its_plane_is_refused` (the review repro: D20 x H20 cylinder, cap on a +X stop face)
  - `a_cylinder_cap_mated_on_the_floor_lands_at_the_right_height` (the legal twin; the collision check reads the landed stock)
  - `a_turned_cylinder_cap_on_the_floor_is_judged_by_its_face_and_lands` (a re-fit with new facets goes through the face check)
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::locate_tests::the_fixtures_page_locates_the_stock_on_the_vise`

## Readings

Review fix, head `32102879d` (on the PR base, no merge of main):
- `camcraft-app`: `fixture_locate` 11/11, `fixture_locate_stock` 3/3, `fixture_locate_stock_body` 5/5, `fixture_locate_stock_cylinder` 3/3, `fixture_plate_followups` 4/4, `mcp_setup` 9/9, `mcp_pick` 7/7, `mcp_lay_face` 1/1.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings`: clean. The fix changes no UI code.
- Mutation checks: `face_lands` always true makes `a_cylinder_cap_mated_across_its_plane_is_refused` fail. `face_lands` always false makes `a_turned_cylinder_cap_on_the_floor_is_judged_by_its_face_and_lands` fail. With the rigid-carry shortcut off, all the stock suites above still pass.

First head `c492f7006`:

- `camcraft-app`: `fixture_locate` 11/11, `fixture_locate_stock` 3/3, `fixture_locate_stock_body` 5/5, `fixture_plate_followups` 4/4, `mcp_setup` 9/9, `mcp_pick` 7/7, `mcp_lay_face` 1/1.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: 933 pass, 1 fail. The fail is `stock_fit_controls_follow_the_selected_shape`; it also fails on main (#2170, fix in PR #2171).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick` did not complete in 50 min on a busy machine (my `timeout` stopped it; no test failed). I ran its parts above one by one.
- `one_pick_rule::locate_and_points_drafts_take_box_corners_as_points` now sets the body to Part. Its document has a stock, and the test pins the part corner.

## Not exercised

- A stock locate in a setup with a turned frame (the tests use the default setup frame).
- A cylinder stock with a turn that is not a multiple of the facet angle. The box check refuses it (the turned facets change the box). This refusal is safe, but a user can find it too strict.
- A stock vertex mate after a re-fit (the vertex branch of the check has no test of its own).
- The camcraft-ui suites after the review fix (the fix changes no UI code).

title: fix(sim): simulate a stock held in a vise; model quarter-turned stock
body:
## What changed

- `MoveModel` (and so `LocatePart`) keeps the stock's own rotation when the move does not turn the part. Before, the float noise of the locate solve (about 5e-14) became a stored stock rotation, and the stock sim refused the stock in a vise.
- `stock_follow::sim_frame` is the one law for the stock frame of the simulation. `stock_sim::stock_grid`, `stock_sim_held::first_body` / `first_field` and `stock_view::stock_facets` read it.
  - An unturned stock is unchanged.
  - A box turned by a quarter-turn multiple (within 1e-9) is its unturned twin with the sides swapped.
  - An upright cylinder is an unturned cylinder.
  - A from-model stock is read from its placed mesh at any turn.
  - An oblique box and a laid cylinder are refused by name (`OBLIQUE_STOCK`, `LAID_CYLINDER`).
- The UI says a simulation refusal one time, in plain words. The uncut stock stays drawn.
- Review fix (commit 465638b09): four suites used a stock turned a quarter about Z to make the program sim refuse. The device is now a turn of 1e-6 rad about Z (`OBLIQUE`), which the sim refuses by name. See "Readings".
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2177-square-stock-sim.md`.

## Readings

Effect: a project whose stock had locate noise or a quarter turn was "not judged" by the stock sim. Now the sim judges it, and a gouge that the sim finds can block the post. No posted G-code changes. No golden `.nc` / `.cl` file and no snapshot PNG changes.

The review found 9 red tests. In each case the PR is correct and the test device was wrong:

| Test (suite) | Reading |
|---|---|
| `deep-Engrave-true`, `low-top-Engrave-true`, `wall-Engrave-true` (`engrave_law`) | The cut is a real gouge (the operation convicts it too). The post was refused. The sim now judges the quarter-turned stock, so its gouge clause leads the message. |
| `through` and `stock-through` / `stock-web` Engrave (`mark_floor` lines 160, 253) | Same: a cut through the 2 mm plate. The sim convicts it correctly. |
| `into-a-trace-true` (`neighbour_law`) | Same: the flank enters part A by 0.3 mm. The sim finds 0.3 mm on A, as on the aligned stock. |
| `low-stock-face-true`, `slot-false-true`, `engrave-false-true` (`stock_source_law`) | Same: cuts off the stock into the part. |

The `by_op` checks are kept and are not loosened. They pin that the operation's own gouge blocks the post when the sim does not judge. Each `by_op` check now also asserts that the sim refuses the stock with `OBLIQUE_STOCK`, so the device cannot become silent. The fixture box check takes 1e-4 mm in X and Y for the 1e-6 rad turn (the corners move by less than 6e-5 mm). Z stays at 1e-9.

## Pinning tests

- `stock_in_vise_sim` (2 tests): a located stock in a vise is simulated; an oblique stock is refused by name.
- New, one in each suite: `a_quarter_turned_stock_is_judged_by_the_program_sim` in `engrave_law`, `mark_floor`, `neighbour_law`, `stock_source_law`. The quarter-turned stock is judged, its gouge blocks the post, and a legal mark posts.
- The MCP parity test of `stock_source_law` moved to the new suite `stock_source_law_mcp` (the 400-line law). The `#[test]` count grows by 4: 28 to 32 in the five suites.

## Gate (on the PR head, not merged with main)

- `engrave_law` 10/10, `mark_floor` 7/7, `neighbour_law` 7/7, `stock_source_law` 7/7, `stock_source_law_mcp` 1/1.
- `stock_in_vise_sim` 2/2, `post_not_judged` 4/4, `area_controls` 13/13, `pocket_recognition` 11/11 (they share the changed test modules).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The review run (trial merge with main `1f15f98e7`) covers the rest: app lib 353, ui lib 949 and 13 ui suites, `stock_sim_document`, `stock_view`, `rotary_field_parity`, `posting`, `verify`, `stock_source_verdict`.

## Not exercised

- No run on a real control or machine.
- No GUI run for this fix.
- Not built merged with the current `main`: the PR merges cleanly, and the current `main` has a debug build error in work by a different agent.
- The combination with PR #2184 (`fixture_locate_stock`, `fixture_locate_stock_body`, `stock_in_vise_sim`) is not run. Run them after the second of the two merges.

Changelog: The simulation now shows and judges a stock held in a vise after a locate, and a stock turned by a quarter turn; a stock turned off the machine axes is refused in plain words.

Effort: high

Fixes #2177

- New `JudgedOutline::with_drawn(drawn, stored)`. It refuses (`OutlineError::PastJudged`) a drawn point outside every band at its height, and a stored cutter that is wider or longer than the judged one. The picture is never wider than the check.

title: feat(machine): define AC trunnion kinematics fields and non-RTCP flag
body:
Stacked on #2126 (merge #2126 first)

## What changed
- Added `AxisLimits.parent`, `AxisLimits.chain_order`, `pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover`, and `sign_convention` in `crates/post/src/machine/def.rs` and `crates/post/src/machine/trunnion.rs`, keeping `Machine.axes` sorted by controller coordinate while `Machine::rotary_axes()` returns rotaries in `kinematics.default.parts` parent-child order.
- Updated `collect_axes` and `parse_mch_with` in `crates/post/src/machine/parse.rs` to parse optional unit-scaled `pivot`/`offset` lengths, degree `zero_offset`, boolean `rollover`, `controller.rtcp`, and `sign_convention` (`tool_rh` | `table_rh`) under the unstated-limit rule.
- Wired `trunnion_refusals` into `crates/app/src/machine/validate.rs` so invalid vectors, mismatched types, disagreeing `sign_convention`, or rotary keys on linear parts fail by name in both `parse_mch` and `validate_text`.
- Extracted rotary/RTCP mirroring into `crates/post/src/post/machine_rotary.rs` so `mirror()` and `script_props()` honor `controller.rtcp = false`, emit `signConvention` (default `tool_rh`), and pass the ordered rotary chain to post scripts.
- Guarded `tilt(p)` in `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps` to refuse tilted moves on multi-rotary machines when controller RTCP is false even if rotary clamp codes exist, matching `fanuc.cps`.
- Bumped `PROJECT_VERSION` from 65 to 66 in `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` after preserving the v64/v65 barriers from main and documented trunnion schema semantics in `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs` and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`.
- Recorded architectural choices in `docs/decisions/1962-trunnion-schema.md`.

## Cause
The `.mch` schema, validator, and post mirror had no representation for trunnion pivot/offset geometry, zero offset, rollover, parent-child chain order independent of `ctrl_coord` sorting, explicit `tool_rh`/`table_rh` sign convention, or an explicit `controller.rtcp: false` override. Non-vertical rotary axes always inferred controller RTCP geometrically, risking `G43.4` emission on non-RTCP trunnion controls.

## Break-through controls before and after

These captures use the real Heights parameter controls in the headless egui renderer.
The before captures use `holes_page.rs` from `2ab7ae424^`, before the Break-through rows.
Only ignored bindings for the new model fields were added to compile that page.
The after captures use the current page. Thread uses an internal thread in both captures.

## Tests
- Pins (`crates/post/tests/trunnion_schema.rs`, 0/4 passed before fix, 4/4 passed after final edit): `explicit_non_rtcp_trunnion_does_not_promise_controller_compensation`, `rotary_chain_order_preserved_when_controller_coordinates_differ`, `trunnion_fields_parse_and_mirror_with_unit_scaling`, `invalid_trunnion_fields_refuse_by_name`.
- Pins (`crates/app/tests/trunnion_schema.rs`, 0/2 passed before fix, 2/2 passed after final edit): `validator_accepts_ac_trunnion_and_refuses_bad_fields_by_name`, `project_roundtrips_non_rtcp_trunnion_and_protects_version`.
- Targeted app suites (`cargo test -p camcraft-app --test index_swing --test index_swing_horizontal --test trunnion_schema`): 13 + 13 + 2 passed.
- Mutation 1: removed `chain_order` sorting in `crates/post/src/machine/trunnion.rs` (`rotary_axes`): `rotary_chain_order_preserved_when_controller_coordinates_differ` and `trunnion_fields_parse_and_mirror_with_unit_scaling` failed; restored and all 4 passed.
- Mutation 2: reverted `crates/post/src/post/machine.rs`: 3/4 tests in `post::trunnion_schema` failed; restored and passed.
- Mutation 3: reverted `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: `explicit_non_rtcp_trunnion_does_not_promise_controller_compensation` failed; restored and passed.
- Mutation 4: reverted `crates/app/src/machine/validate.rs`: `validator_accepts_ac_trunnion_and_refuses_bad_fields_by_name` failed; restored and passed.
- Mutation 5: reverted `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` to `base-2126`: `project_roundtrips_non_rtcp_trunnion_and_protects_version` failed; restored and passed.

Add optional AC trunnion kinematics fields, rotary chain order, explicit sign convention, and `controller.rtcp` flag to the `.mch` schema and post mirror.

title: feat(import): open Solidcraft .sc designs as a model
body:
Needs maintainer: adds the native camcraft-geometry -> camcraft-kernel dependency (decision file included).

Branch base: upstream/main af83da0f.

## What changed
- CamCraft opens a Solidcraft `.sc` design as a model. The app reads the cached final body of the design.
- Model > Open offers `.sc`. A viewport drop takes `.sc`. MCP `import_model` takes `.sc`.
- These three use the one model import. The `Format::Solidcraft` arm in app dispatches to the re-exported `camcraft_geometry::solidcraft` parser.
- The module calls `camcraft_kernel::solidcraft::import_solidcraft`. Then it meshes the body with `camcraft_kernel::machining_mesh::machining_mesh` at the STEP chord cap (0.005 mm).
- A damaged or unsupported `.sc` is refused by name. The message is "Solidcraft design refused: <kernel reason>". The model is not added and the history does not change.
- A watchdog requests cooperative cancellation after 300 seconds. The kernel planner has no cancellation hook. Completion within 300 seconds is not guaranteed.
- A STEP facet budget for a `.sc` is refused by name, as for STL and OBJ.
- The kernel edge is native only. The browser build does not offer `.sc`, and it refuses `.sc` by name.
- `camcraft-kernel` re-exports `CancelToken`, so geometry does not need its own solidcore dependency.
- Open and drop now use one extension list (`state::MODEL_EXTENSIONS`). The drop refusal message comes from that list.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/1456-sc-open.md`. It lists the imported kernel items, why the caller cannot pass the value in, and what rebuilds.

## Review screenshots

Before uses the production UI files from `af83da0f405cfd244f0c9bf8192ab7309e9db824`.
After uses the production UI files from `8ad6817541bd9acf2c917ed0bc57544aab2bec5f`.
The parser move does not change these UI files.

The native Linux captures call the production `mesh_dialog()` through a temporary test entry point.
Only the starting directory is set for the capture. The directory contains the same STL, Solidcraft, and text files.
The GTK portal applies the real Mesh filter. Before hides the Solidcraft file. After shows it.

The kernel reader from #1464 and #1474 is in main. No code in `crates/app/src` called it. Thus Model > Open did not offer `.sc`.

## Current verification

Head: `13d33b478a7539271fa2ce0a124009f1759c9bd9`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. Manifest changes select the batch fallback. All 10 steps pass.
- All-target clippy with `-D warnings` on geometry, app, and UI: green through the gate.

title: feat(boundaries)!: add "Do not touch" face/edge protection on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket
body:
Stacked on #2077 (merge #2077 first)

## What changed
- Added **Do not touch** protected faces, patches, and edge chains plus standoff **Clearance** (`>= 0.0` mm, default `0.0`) to `AreaControls` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`, `area.rs`).
- Separated `has_boundary_edits()` from `is_default()` so empty protection preserves legacy toolpaths, boundary clipping, and generation stamps (`op_stamp` hashes `camcraft-do-not-touch-v1` only when protection is active).
- Added independent 3D full-tool keep-out generation and swept verification in `crates/sim/src/verify/` (`avoid.rs`, `avoid_poly.rs`, `avoid_links.rs`, `swept.rs`, `probe.rs`, `Warning::AvoidHit`), checking flutes, shank, and holder against `clearance + max(stock_to_leave, 0)` and elevating obstructed rapid traverses.
- Wired per-level keep-outs, `KeepDown` link chord checks (`prev_center` / `prev_state`), and impossible-room refusals into `2D Offset` (`machining2d::pocket_avoid`) and `3D Pocket` (`machining3d::pocket3d_avoid`, `shell.rs`, `ladder.rs`, `entry.rs`), plus upright `route_links` and upright/tilted `verify_avoid` in `generate.rs`.
- Added live post-gate checks (`live_avoid_problems` in `posting.rs`) so violated or stale/overlapping protected items block NC posting.
- Added undoable `SetOperationDoNotTouch`, overlap and vertex validation across `EditOperationParams`, `SetOperationGeometry`, `ChangeOperationKind`, and `EditOperationLinks`, MCP tools `get_operation_do_not_touch` / `set_operation_do_not_touch`, and refused non-default `"Do not touch"` on unsupported operation kinds by name.
- Rendered `"Do not touch"` UI controls, rows with `"×"` remove + viewport hover highlight, and persistent selection viewport overlays (`crates/ui/src/avoid_viz.rs`, `egui_app/boundary.rs`, `boundary_draft.rs`).
- Bumped `PROJECT_VERSION` `63 -> 64` (stacked on `#2077`) so pre-v64 readers refuse files carrying `"do_not_touch"` rather than ignoring protection.
- Updated `site/content/guide/` docs, `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, and `docs/decisions/2055-do-not-touch.md`.

title: fix(ui): world gizmo hides Y on a lathe without a Y axis
body:
Supersedes #2036

GitHub closed #2036 when its parent #2023 merged and its base branch was deleted. This PR has the same branch.

## Merge of main

- `git merge origin/main` was clean (no conflicts, no hand edits in the merge).
- The fix commit cfadf347b wrote `crates/ui/src/interact.rs` with CRLF line ends. The diff showed each line of that file as changed. Commit 6a800e5ce restores LF. The content does not change. The diff of `interact.rs` against main is now 14 lines added and 2 lines removed.
- Main does not compile `camcraft-ui` at this time: `crates/ui/src/machine_modes.rs` `short_caption` has no arm for `MachineKind::Waterjet` (E0004). This PR does not fix that. For the test run, I added the arm locally and did not commit it.

## What changed
- The world gizmo draws only the axes that the machine has.
- A mill shows X, Y and Z.
- A lathe shows Z and X. It shows Y only when its machine file states a linear Y axis.
- A mill-turn keeps the milling frame, as #2023 does. It hides Y only when its file states axes and none is a linear Y. An unstated axis list hides nothing.
- The change reuses the view frame of #2023. There is no second derivation of the lathe orientation. The new `view_frame::axes_shown` only filters the axis lines and the axis letters.
- Display only. The WCS, the toolpaths and the posted G-code do not read it.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2019-lathe-gizmo.md` (mill-turn rule).

body:
## What changed
- Split work-offset frame classification (`OffsetFrame::Yaw` vs tilted `OffsetFrame::Rotated`) in `crates/app/src/posting_wcs_rotation.rs`.
- Carry pure Z-axis WCS rotation into milling toolpath generation via `WcsYaw` (`crates/app/src/operation/wcs_yaw.rs`, `generate.rs`, `job.rs`, `stamp.rs`, `drill_prior.rs`), `SlotBound::rotated_xy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room.rs`), and `Dexel::rotated_z_conservative` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel.rs`).
- Rotate generated `Toolpath`, `Region`, and located errors back to Setup table frame `S` before simulation, verification, workholding checks, fixture linking, and machine travel limit checks.
- Add `WcsRotationOutput` (`Bake` default, `Control` opt-in) across schema, project DTOs, posting, MCP `set_post_options`, setup sheet, and the Post Options UI (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`, `posting.rs`, `project/*`, `mcp/post_options_tools.rs`, `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_options.rs`).
- Add `crates/post/src/post/wcs_rotate.rs` and `controller.coordinate_rotation` / `wcsRotation` capability checks across `.mch` and five `.cps` posts (`fanuc`, `haas`, `mazak`, `doosan-dnm` emit `G68`/`G69`; `sinumerik` emits `ROT RPL=`/`ROT`).
- Refuse probing, turning, EDM, 5-axis/3+2 moves, and XZ/YZ arcs under a Z-rotated WCS, and guard `Align WCS (3-2-1)` against tilted faces on `Kind::Mill` (`crates/app/src/setup_wcs_tilt.rs`, `crates/ui/src/vertex_pick.rs`, `geo_page.rs`).

## Cause
Milling strategy generators and rest-prior grids ran directly in setup table coordinates `S`, ignoring any Z rotation on the setup WCS. Posting also rejected every rotated offset unconditionally regardless of whether only Z yaw was present.

## Tests
- Pins (`crates/post/tests/wcs_rotate.rs`): `bake_keeps_setup_table_coordinates_without_g68`, `control_mode_emits_g68_or_rot_only_when_machine_and_post_declare_it`, `mch_parser_reads_optional_controller_coordinate_rotation`, `probing_or_non_xy_arc_under_rotated_wcs_refuses_by_name`, `five_axis_abc_move_in_rotated_wcs_refuses_by_name`.

- Pins (`crates/app/tests/rotated_wcs.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_align_guard_tests.rs`, plus `mcp_post_options.rs` and `setup_post_options.rs`): `the_post_stream_carries_z_offset_rotation`, `a_tilted_work_offset_is_refused_by_name`, `the_setup_sheet_states_the_offset_rotation`, `align_wcs_321_refuses_tilted_side_face_on_mill_and_names_part_alignment`, `align_wcs_321_allows_top_face_with_z_yaw_on_mill`.

title: feat(app)!: place a DXF profile on a setup's stock - Sketch entity, ImportDxf, import_dxf MCP tool
body:
Stacked on #2106 (sketch chaining, issue 1861). Merge #2106 first. This branch now merges upstream `main` and keeps both project modules and the breakthrough fields from #1557.

## What changed

A DXF drawing is now a profile that the user places on the stock of a setup. It is not a model. This follows the scope change of the maintainer on issue 1862 (2026-11-15).

- **`Sketch` component** (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`, registered in `register_schema`). It holds the setup and the shared drawing data. The entity has no `Facets`, and `model::is_model` is false for it. No 3D solid tool reads it as a mesh.
- **`camcraft_geometry::sketch_data::SketchData`**: the primitives in mm, the layer names, the source units, the join tolerance, the chains of issue 1861 and the import summary. The chains are always made from the stored primitives.
- **Placement** (`crates/app/src/sketch.rs`): the `Location` of a profile is relative to the top face of the stock of its setup, at the stock origin. A profile has Z 0 and a turn about the face normal only. A moved or resized stock carries the profile.
- **`ImportDxf::new(world, setup, path, options)`** (undoable). It gets the setup as an argument (`None`: the active setup). It refuses at construction: a setup with no stock, an unknown setup, a file that is not `.dxf`, a malformed DXF, a drawing with nothing to place, a name in use. A file with no `$INSUNITS` (absent or 0) and no unit from the caller gives the typed `CommandError::DxfUnitsMissing { width, height }`.
- **`MoveSketch::new(world, name, x, y, angle_deg)`** (undoable): the move and the turn on the stock face.
- **`DeleteEntity`** restores a profile on undo. **`SelectEntity`** works on a profile. **`MoveModel`** and **`DeleteSetup`** refuse a profile by name.
- **Virtual model reference** (`crates/app/src/sketch_model.rs`): it is derived from the world when a setup has a placed profile and the document has no part. Nothing is stored for it.
- **Project file**: entity kind `sketch` with a `sketch` key; `PROJECT_VERSION` 66 -> 67. The chains are made again on load.
- **MCP**: `import_dxf` and `move_dxf_profile`. `get_job` lists `profiles`, gives each setup a `model_reference`, and gives an operation on a profile `checks_against`. **Script**: `cam.importDxf(path, { setup, units, join_tol, name })`.
- `docs/decisions/1862-sketch-profile.md` records the design of the virtual reference: what it is in the ECS, what the project file stores, and which checks read it.

## How each point of the scope change is met

1. A profile is not a model: `is_model` is false, `model_entities` does not list it, `get_job` lists it under `profiles`.
2. A setup with a stock and no model is legal: the tests make a sheet stock, place the profile and add an operation.
3. The `Sketch` belongs to the setup. Its `Location` is relative to the stock top face at the stock origin. `MoveSketch` moves and turns it on that face.
4. `ImportDxf` gets the setup. Undo removes the profile. The MCP tool and the script verb get the same argument.
5. The virtual model reference is `sketch_model::of(world, setup)`. The source door of the operation commands accepts a profile as a source. The model-height diagnostic names the reference. `sketch_model::model_loaded` is the question for the operation pages of issue 1863. The reference has no facets.
6. No check passes silently. An operation on a profile states what it is checked against (the stock and the chains of the profile). A kind that needs a solid model refuses a profile by name. A 3D kind in a setup with a virtual reference refuses by name. Generation of an operation on a profile refuses by name (see the open questions).
7. The decision file is in this PR.

## Project file version

This PR writes **version 67**. Current upstream `main` writes version 66 for the trunnion schema from #1962. Profiles take the next version. Main's trunnion fields, v65-to-v66 migration and earlier steps stay intact, and the v66-to-v67 profile step needs no data rewrite. Stated `controller_rtcp: false` and trunnion data remain intact, as do tilt bases, earlier cutting-data rows and breakthrough values. A v62 file still loads through the earlier migration (`a_v62_file_steps_up_unchanged`). Tests check v63 breakthrough and v64 cutting-data files through load, save as v67, and load again. The v65 tilt pins retain legacy basis 0 and basis 1 through load, save, and reload. The new v66 trunnion pin checks the stated machine data through load, save, and reload. The profile and rest payloads also survive a v67 save and load.

## Open design questions

These need a decision of the maintainer. This PR does the part that is specified and does not guess the rest.

1. **Toolpath from the chains.** The added "Done means" says that the setup "accepts a 2D operation on the sketch chains". This PR accepts the operation at each command door (create, paste, retarget, retype, move to a setup). It does not generate a toolpath from the chains: issue 1864 has that work (chain picks, side per chain, checks without a mesh). Until then, generation refuses by name and says what the operation is checked against. Is that the correct split, or must #1862 also generate?
2. **Top of Model and Bottom of Model on a virtual reference.** A reference with no solid has no top and no bottom. This PR refuses these heights by name (the text tells the user to use a stock or fixed height). The alternative is to give them a value, for example the stock top and the stock bottom. That changes cut depths, so it is not decided here.
3. **"The stock origin".** This PR reads it as the origin of the stock entity. For a box and a cylinder that is the centre in XY. The alternative is a corner of the stock or the WCS origin.
4. **Which kinds take a profile.** This PR admits the 2D milling, plasma and wire EDM sections. Drilling (holes from DXF circles), turning and sinker EDM refuse a profile by name. Is that the correct set?
5. **`MoveSketch` and not `MoveModel`.** The issue body said `MoveModel`. A profile has a face placement (X, Y, angle), and `MoveModel` writes a world placement and carries the stock. This PR adds `MoveSketch`, and `MoveModel` refuses a profile by name.
6. **A profile that is larger than the stock, or off its edge,** is not refused at placement. Issue 1864 has the check of the chains against the stock.

title: feat(ai): provider HTTP clients, keychain keys and offline-only mode
body:
**New third-party crates - needs the maintainer's decision (`needs-maintainer`):**

| Crate | Version | Licence | Why the workspace's existing deps can't do it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reqwest` | 0.12.28 (default features off, `rustls-tls`) | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | Provides an async HTTP request that cancellation can interrupt. Redirects and environment proxies are disabled. |
| `tokio` | 1.52.3 (`rt`, `time`, `net`, `macros`) | MIT | Runs each request on a current-thread runtime inside the chat worker. Cancellation drops the active request future. |
| `rustls` / `rustls-webpki` / `rustls-pki-types` | 0.23.46 / 0.103.17 / 1.16.0 (via reqwest) | Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT / ISC / MIT OR Apache-2.0 | TLS for the https cloud APIs; no OpenSSL on Linux. |
| `ring` + `untrusted` | 0.17.14 / 0.9.0 (via rustls) | Apache-2.0 AND ISC / ISC | rustls's crypto (C/asm, built by `cc`; no CMake, unlike aws-lc-rs). |
| `webpki-roots` | 1.0.12 | CDLA-Permissive-2.0 | The Mozilla CA roots, so the build needs no system trust store. |
| `keyring` + `keyring-core` | 4.2.0 / 1.0.1 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | Nothing in the tree reaches an OS credential store. |
| keyring stores: `apple-native-keyring-store` (+ `security-framework`), `windows-native-keyring-store`, `zbus-secret-service-keyring-store` (+ `secret-service`) | 1.x | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Secret Service. The Linux store rides the `zbus` 5 **already in the lock** - pure Rust, no `libdbus` build package. |
| RustCrypto `aes`, `cbc`, `cipher`, `hkdf`, `hmac`, `sha2`, `digest`, `subtle`, `zeroize`, ... (via secret-service) | various | MIT OR Apache-2.0 (`subtle` BSD-3-Clause) | Secret Service session encryption. |

`url` 2.5 was **already in Cargo.lock** and is now a direct dependency of `camcraft-app` (endpoint parsing with the same URL parser reqwest uses). All new crates are under `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]` of `camcraft-app` only; the browser build links none of them. Notices added to `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`. The review fix replaces blocking `ureq` with `reqwest` and a current-thread `tokio` runtime so cancellation interrupts active requests. Considered and dropped: detached blocking requests (they keep the socket and worker alive), `native-tls` (OpenSSL headers on Linux), keyring's dbus store (vendored libdbus C build) - see `docs/decisions/1945-ai-provider-clients.md`.

## What changed

- **`camcraft_app::ai`** (new, `crates/app/src/ai/`):
  - `endpoint` - URL parse (WHATWG `url`; user info, query and fragment refused), loopback test (`localhost`, 127/8, `::1`, IPv4-mapped), `admit` (offline-only reaches loopback alone; plain `http://` off the machine is refused, key or not), `admit_addrs` (the resolver's half).
  - `presets` - Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (GPT and Codex), Gemini `generateContent` (all `https://`); Ollama `http://localhost:11434/v1`, Unsloth Studio `http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`, LM Studio `http://localhost:1234/v1`, llama.cpp `llama-server` `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` (`--jinja` named in the label).
  - `wire` - the request path and body per provider. Tool-call envelopes are echoed in each provider's own shape (Anthropic content blocks, Chat `tool_calls` message, Responses `output` items incl. reasoning, Gemini content incl. `thoughtSignature`); consecutive tool results merge into one Anthropic user message / one Gemini turn. Model ids are checked so they cannot add a query or climb the Gemini path. Fallback (prompt-JSON / Q&A) payloads go into the system prompt with no tools.
  - `probe` - Ollama `/api/show` capabilities -> tools / vision / fallback mode.
  - `secret` - `ApiKey` has no `Display` and a redacted `Debug`, refuses control characters (no header injection); lookup is the env var (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`) first, then the keychain.
  - `http` (native only) - the client. `admit` runs before anything resolves; the agent's resolver refuses non-loopback addresses when offline-only or plain http; **no redirects followed**, **no proxy from the environment**, connect/total timeouts, auth only in headers (`x-api-key`, `Authorization: Bearer`, `x-goog-api-key`), errors carry the host, status and the provider's message - never the key.
  - `keychain` (native only) - `load` / `store` / `forget` under the service `camcraft-ai`.
- **`prefs.json`** gains `aiOfflineOnly` (written only when on); `ViewPrefs` has no field that could hold a key.
- **AI Chat dock** (`crates/ui`): native builds use the new `transport_http::HttpTransport` (presets map to the endpoints above; the key comes from env/keychain or the step is refused by name; an Ollama model without the `tools` capability is refused by name in the native-tools preset, pointing at the Prompt-JSON / Q&A presets). The "Offline only" switch is restored from and saved to `prefs.json`. The browser build keeps the offline-only `DefaultTransport` (now `cfg(wasm32)`).

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/ai_http.rs` against a fake loopback HTTP server (no real key: a fixed placeholder sent only to 127.0.0.1): `anthropic_messages_wire_format`, `openai_chat_completions_wire_format`, `openai_responses_wire_format`, `gemini_generate_content_wire_format`, `local_runtimes_send_no_auth_header`, `ollama_capability_probe`, `offline_only_blocks_every_non_loopback_host_before_a_socket` (every cloud preset plus TEST-NET / private / IPv6 hosts refused in < 500 ms, plus the resolver check), `plain_http_off_this_machine_is_refused`, `redirects_are_not_followed_and_errors_never_carry_the_key`. 9/9 pass.
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs::offline_only_survives_and_the_file_stores_zero_keys` (the file's keys are exactly the known five; no "key"/"token"/"secret"/"password"/"bearer").
- Unit tests in `ai::endpoint`, `ai::presets`, `ai::secret`, `ai::wire`, `ai::probe`, and `transport_http::every_panel_preset_has_an_endpoint`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (fell back to batch: Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock changed): geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app (incl. `ai_http`, `view_prefs`) and ui suites all **ok** (35.5 min). Clippy `-D warnings` FAILS only on `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs:115` `MIN_LABEL_PX` never used - pre-existing on upstream main since PR #2095, tracked in #2104 / PR #2111; no other lint in the touched crates.
- `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (with `web/build-app-wasm.sh`'s wasi sysroot and flecs patch): **Finished** clean; the only warnings are pre-existing unused imports in `ai_chat/worker.rs` (untouched here).

## Not exercised

- No call to a real provider or a real local runtime (no key in tests, no network in tests).
- The OS keychain itself (`keychain::load/store/forget`) is not called by any test - a test would prompt or write the developer's real keychain; the lookup order is pinned with an injected keychain.
- No UI for entering/storing a key yet: keys come from the env vars, or from the keychain if stored by other means (service `camcraft-ai`, account `anthropic`/`openai`/`gemini`). A key-entry field is a follow-up.
- Streaming responses (each step is one complete response, as the dock's worker expects).

Changelog: AI Chat reaches Anthropic, OpenAI (Chat and Responses), Gemini over https and Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio and llama-server on loopback; API keys come only from the environment or the OS keychain; "Offline only" is saved and blocks every non-loopback host in the HTTP client (#1945)
Effort: high (not escalated)
Process change: no
Fork: mkinney fork, branched from upstream/main 780b0a25a

Fixes #1945

The images show the actual egui shell with the Local Q&A preset and Offline only enabled.

title: test(motion): pin the rest Adaptive raster entry proof and the D/80 load ceiling
body:
**Stacked on #2112** (rest Adaptive, `mkinney:issue/2031-rest-adaptive`, head 71a7fee47). This PR's own change is its last commit (c234093ee); until #2112 merges the diff against main shows #2112's commits too. Merge #2112 first.

## What changed

Tests only (no product code): three pins the M5 review of #2112 found missing.

- **Raster half of the entry proof** - `machining2d::adaptive::rest::tests::the_raster_half_of_the_entry_proof_refuses_on_its_own` (unit test, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/rest/tests.rs`). It hands `Entries` a raster holding a 1 mm pillar that the polygon bound does not hold, then asks for a plunge whose rim would stand 0.2 mm inside the pillar: refused. A plunge clear of the pillar by more than the margin is still proved. Inside the planner the raster comes from the same polygon bound (grown), and the polygon half refuses everything the raster would, so no planner fixture can make the raster refuse on its own. The test therefore works on `Entries` directly.
  - Mutation-checked: removing `&& self.stock.air(p, p, self.footprint)` from `Entries::proved` turns it red, and so does `footprint: 0.0`.
- **Load ceiling on the default D/80 measuring grid** - `on_the_default_measuring_grid_the_load_stays_under_its_documented_ceiling` (`crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`). Optimal x 1.2 (`LOAD_CEILING_D80` in `sim.rs`, with its readings documented), on the climb 3 mm corners and on the conventional 3.5 mm corners with 0.3 mm left.
- **Corner assertion on a fine grid (D/240)** - `on_a_fine_grid_the_corners_read_within_the_planning_margin`. A 26 x 22 pocket with 3.5 mm corners, cut conventionally with 0.3 mm left. On the measuring stock that is 1680 x 1440 cells, under the 4096-cell cap. It must read within the planner's own margin (optimal x 1.05), and every feed stays in the corners.
- `sim.rs`: `Sim::on_grid(region, cell)` and `assert_load_within(reading, slack)`. `assert_load_held` is now `assert_load_within(.., LOAD_SLACK)`.
- `docs/decisions/2113-rest-adaptive-pins.md`.

## Readings (debug, optimal load 14.6% of D)

| Fixture | D/80 | D/120 | D/240 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 x 40, 3 mm corners, climb | 14.6% | 13.1% | - |
| 60 x 40, 3.5 mm corners, conventional, 0.3 mm left | 16.7% | 14.7% | - |
| 26 x 22, 3.5 mm corners, conventional, 0.3 mm left | 14.6% | - | 12.7% |
| two bays, 10 mm neck | 15.0% | 15.0% | - |

No real bug showed up. The D/80 excess is the measuring rim taking in wall in a concave corner: the same paths read lower on finer grids.

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: motion suites ok (396 s), app suites ok (213 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The three new tests, one by one, plus the two mutations above (each red, then reverted).

## Not exercised

- Windows/Linux: run on macOS only.
- The island and neck fixtures on D/240: too large for the cap.

Changelog: none
Effort: medium (worked by issue-worker-high; not escalated)

Fixes #2113

title: refactor(log): library and UI diagnostics become tracing events
body:
## What changed

The last slice of #163, after PR #222 (app seams: save/open/post/generate/commands) and PR #969 (app library eprintln!s and the budget-refusal events). With this, no diagnostic in the library or UI crates bypasses the one `tracing` subscriber any more.

- **Library crates** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): every non-test `eprintln!` is now a `tracing` event - refusals and fallbacks at `warn` (refused move/builder axis or C angle; multi-axis moves held vertical or radial, a rotary start on the axis, a degenerate drive curve skipped; a non-finite sim path left out or move held still; the dual iso-surface falling back to marching tetrahedra; a missing starter tool catalog), the opt-in `CAMCRAFT_PROFILE_PROJECTION` profile lines at `info`. The text of each line is unchanged.
- **Standalone bins** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): each installs a stderr subscriber with the app's filter rule (`CAMCRAFT_LOG`, else `RUST_LOG`, else `info`), so the converted library warnings still reach their terminal. Their own `println!` reports and usage errors are the CLI's answer and stay as they are.
- **UI**: the `diag` seam (#31) now emits `tracing` events natively (target `camcraft_ui`, `warn`/`info`) instead of `eprintln!`/`println!`; wasm32 still goes to the browser console. The native window (`shell_window.rs`, `shell_window/frame.rs`), GPU bring-up (`gpu_init.rs`), Cmd+Q hook (`os_quit.rs`) and the headless proof (`shell.rs`) now speak through the seam, so the law test's allow-list shrinks to the seam and test-only code (`gpu.rs`'s test module, `headless_gpu.rs`'s `device_for_test`, whose "SKIPPED - NOT a pass" line must show in a test run with no subscriber).

**Dependencies.** No new crate: `tracing` and `tracing-subscriber` are already workspace dependencies (root `Cargo.toml`, since PR #222) and in `Cargo.lock`; this PR adds `{ workspace = true }` lines for them to the five library crates and `tracing` (plus `tracing-subscriber` as a dev-dependency) to `camcraft-ui`. `Cargo.lock` gains only those dependency edges. No `camcraft-*` edge is added. Decision record: `docs/decisions/163-tracing-libs.md`.

The issue's "Done means" is now covered across the three PRs: post writes name the file and result or why not (#222), a generation budget names its limit (#969, `a_budget_refusal_names_the_limit_that_fired_at_warn`), levels come from `CAMCRAFT_LOG`/`RUST_LOG` with a quiet `info` default (#222), and the library/UI prints that bypassed the filter are gone (this PR). No event was added inside a hot loop (the geometry profile lines stay behind their env var).

## How tested

- New pinning tests:
  - `camcraft-cl` `tests/refusal_log.rs::a_refused_axis_or_angle_is_a_warning_under_the_cl_target` - a refused move axis, C angle and builder axis are each a `WARN` event under `camcraft_cl`, and a stricter filter silences them.
  - `camcraft-ui` `diag::tests::diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` - `diag_warn!`/`diag_info!` are `WARN`/`INFO` events under `camcraft_ui`, and a filter below them stays quiet.
  - `camcraft-ui` `diag::tests::shared_ui_code_prints_only_through_the_diag_seam` (existing law, allow-list tightened).
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`; Cargo changes fall back to batch scope): green on every test step in 27.9 min (geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, ui suites all ok). The clippy step fails only on the pre-existing `MIN_LABEL_PX is never used` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs:115` (upstream main, #2104, not touched here); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings -A dead_code` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The wasm32 build of the UI was not run (the diag wasm branch is unchanged).
- The real GPU window and the Windows GUI-subsystem console were not launched by hand; the converted lines are the same text through the same seam.

title: feat(tools): convert STEP bodies to DXF half-profiles and import/export DXF
body:
## What changed

- Added a clean-room ASCII DXF writer in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/writer.rs` (`dxf::write`, `dxf::write_bytes`, `Unit::code`) emitting `HEADER` (`$INSUNITS`), `TABLES` (`LAYER`), and `ENTITIES` (`LINE`, `ARC`, `CIRCLE`).
- Added conservative stepped-band reduction in `crates/tools/src/spun_envelope.rs` (`SpunProfile::conservative_from_bands`) merging adjacent `HolderBand`s strictly upward (`max(r)`) down to at most 31 bands (`<= 64` points) and `MIN_SEGMENT`.
- Added STEP and `ToolBody` <-> ASCII DXF half-profile conversion and DXF import in `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf.rs` and `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf_import.rs` with explicit `CENTRELINE` and `PROFILE` layers.
- Added undoable `SetToolBody` constructors (`from_dxf_bytes`, `from_dxf`, `from_step_profile`, `from_placed_profile`, `profile_dxf`) in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body_dxf.rs` over `tool_body::build_spun`.
- Registered MCP tools `import_tool_holder_dxf`, `export_tool_holder_dxf`, and `convert_tool_step_to_profile` in `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_dxf_tools.rs`.
- Added conservative-envelope and half-profile-only notices, `Import DXF…`, `Export DXF…`, `Import STEP…`, and Body tab `Convert to profile` in `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs`, `tool_profile_page.rs`, and `tool_body_page.rs`.
- Recorded architectural trade-offs in `docs/decisions/743-step-dxf-half-profile.md`.

## Cause

- Direct conversion from `HolderProfile::envelope` to `SpunProfile` failed above 31 stepped bands because `2 * 32 + 2 = 66` exceeds `MAX_POINTS` (`64`).
- CamCraft lacked an ASCII DXF writer and could not export or re-import tool holder half-profiles with an explicit centreline or enforce ISO 13399 CSYS alignment on STEP-to-profile conversion.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `camcraft-geometry::dxf_writer`: `write_and_parse_round_trip_lines_arcs_circles_layers_and_units`, `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name` (2 passed).
  - `camcraft-tools::spun::envelope::tests::thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile` (6 passed): `step_to_dxf_half_profile_envelops_every_sampled_mesh_point`, `non_revolved_step_or_fine_32_plus_band_mesh_is_conservatively_enveloped`, `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`, `dxf_half_profile_import_with_lines_and_arcs_lands_as_tool_body`, `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`, `round_trip_step_to_dxf_to_body_to_dxf_is_stable_within_tolerance`.
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile_mcp`: `mcp_holder_dxf_and_step_profile_tools_list_round_trip_undo_and_refuse` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-ui::egui_app::tests::tool_profile` (9 passed, adding `profile_tab_states_conservative_envelope_and_half_profile_rules_and_dxf_workflow` and `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`).
- Mutations (each tested red after weakening the guard and green after restore):
  - `spun_envelope::join` `max(r)` -> `min(r)`: failed `thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile`; restored green.
  - `dxf::writer` zero-length `LINE` guard bypassed: failed `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name`; restored green.
  - `tool_profile_dxf_import` centreline-crossing guard bypassed: failed `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`; restored green.
  - `step_to_spun_profile` ISO 13399 requirement replaced with `+Z` fallback: failed `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`; restored green.
  - `convert_body_draft_to_profile` clear-axis check bypassed: failed `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`; restored green.
- Gate:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` expanded to the `batch` tier (`crates/geometry/src/dxf/mod.rs` is a shared crate) and passed all 10 steps in 39.8 min with 0 failures (`geometry`, `kernel`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, `app`, `ui`, `clippy -D warnings`).

## Goldens moved

- None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Native OS file-picker modal calls (`import_profile_dxf_dialog`, `export_profile_dxf_dialog`, `import_step_profile_dialog`) delegate to desktop `rfd`; headless UI tests exercise `import_profile_dxf_from`, `export_profile_dxf_to`, `import_step_profile_from`, and `Convert to profile`.
- Release-tier `SLOW_BINARIES` (`motion:finish3d`, `motion:pivot5d`, `motion:flow`, `app:center_cut_multiaxis`) were outside the `batch` gate run.

## Overlaps

- `#2092` (stacked on `#2054`) edits different functions in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs` (`library_body`, `SetToolBody::spun`), `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs` (`sync_tool_profile_ui`, `pick_library_holder`, `run_set_tool_holder`, `editor_library_holder`), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_profile_page.rs` (lines 84-87), and `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` (lines 32, 38, 281); this PR uses `tool_body::build_spun` (no `ToolBody` struct literals) and companion modules/tail blocks; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2096` edits `envelope` and `preview_3d` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_body_page.rs`, different lines from `Convert to profile`; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2077` edits `crates/app/src/lib.rs` line 118 and `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` line 281, different lines from our additions at `lib.rs` and the tail of `all()` in `mcp/tools.rs`; whichever merges second refreshes.


## UI screenshots

Rendered with the real egui shell harness at 1600 × 1200. Before uses the exact `upstream/main` (`a277dd9d51e7b4488403b946d0a3234b71ba7504`) Profile and Body page sources. After uses this PR's page sources. The Body tab shows the same ISO 13399 STEP fixture in both captures. Native file-picker dialogs were not exercised.
