title: feat(tools)!: a tool's library holder is a reference to the entry
body:
Stacked on #2054 (branch `mkinney:issue/2018-weldon-per-taper`, with `main` merged in for #2029). Merge #2054 first; this diff then shows only the #2016 commits. Fork synced from upstream `main` at c86d6db35.

## What changed

A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a reference to the entry, not a drawn copy of its outline.

- `camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (new, `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs`), carried on `ToolBody::library`.
- `tool_body::build_library` is the one place a reference becomes a shape. `SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool` (stated and machine-default holder), the project loader and the `.camtools` reader call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before. The #828 floor for a machine-default holder is unchanged.
- Files: the tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true` when assumed) is written in place of `body`. Project v62 (the unreleased step the issue names); a `.camtools` file says version 2 when a tool names a library holder.
- Migration: an older file is not rewritten. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a custom drawn profile with the same outline, and a `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder stays the tool's own numbers.
- Refusals by tool name: an entry the library does not hold, a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon"), lengths the entry cannot take, a holder that reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, `holder` beside `body`. No other holder is put in its place.
- MCP: `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference; the reply and `get_job` show it as `holder.library`. `add_tool` refuses a `holder` reference inside `definition`; `edit_tool` refuses a `holder` patch. Skill rows updated.
- UI: with a referenced holder the tool settings show the holder diameter and length the laws read as text, not as two fields. The Profile tab names the entry and the picker shows it. The unchanged outline applied again keeps the reference; one edited point makes the holder a custom profile (one undo step).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2016-holder-reference.md`.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on the final head (tools, app and ui suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. macOS (m5).

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/holder_reference.rs`
  - `every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy`: for every library entry, at the default and at other lengths, picked and assumed: the judged tool, envelope, band stack, stamp term and facets equal those of the drawn copy an older build stored, also after a save and load.
  - `an_older_project_loads_as_custom_holders_with_the_same_collision_result`: a v61 project with a drawn copy and a plain holder cylinder loads with the same reads, operation status and warnings (the BT30 flange strikes the fixture wall, hit for hit).
  - `an_older_tool_library_loads_as_custom_holders_and_a_new_one_round_trips_the_reference`
  - `an_unknown_entry_refuses_the_file_by_name_and_never_lands_another_holder` (project and `.camtools`)
  - `a_library_holder_is_the_reference_in_the_document_and_the_file`
  - `the_unchanged_outline_keeps_the_reference_and_an_edited_point_makes_it_custom`
  - `mcp_set_tool_holder_writes_the_reference`
- `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs` unit tests.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_holder_reference.rs`: `a_library_holder_sizes_the_holder_fields_until_its_outline_is_edited`, `the_profile_tab_names_the_entry_and_the_picker_shows_it`.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux. The release tier and the pixel-snapshot lanes (no snapshot PNG changed).
- No real v0.21.0 file was read: the older file in the tests is this build's file rewritten to the older form (`body` with the drawn copy, version 61 / 1).
- The app was not driven by hand.

## Notes for the reviewer

- A build of main between #1453 and this change reads v62 and would drop the `holder` key (development builds only; v0.21.0 refuses v62).
- A corrected library entry now reaches every project that names it. A copy kept the old numbers.
- The tool record's `holder_d`/`holder_len` are not overwritten by the entry (they are what the tool goes back to when the holder is cleared, and writing them would move the stamp). The settings show the entry's numbers.

Changelog: A tool's library holder is stored as a reference to the library entry (name, gauge length, projection) in the project and tool library files, not as a drawn copy; the tool settings show the entry's holder size. Breaking: v0.21.0 and older refuse a file that names a library holder.

Effort: max (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: a project or tool library saved with a library holder states it as a reference (project v62, `.camtools` version 2); v0.21.0 and older refuse such a file.

Process change: yes

Fixes #2016

title: feat(tools)!: cutting data by work material - Unknown default row, stepdown/stepover, stock material
body:
## What changed

Tool cutting data by work material (#2015, part of #2007):

- **`Unknown` row.** Every tool's cutting data now holds an `Unknown` row (file word `unknown`; in code `CuttingRow::material == None`). It is what the tool runs when no row names the material in force, and the fallback for a row's missing stepdown/stepover. It is derived from the tool's own rpm/feed and stored only when it states something more (other numbers, or a step) - so a new tool has it, every older tool reads its own numbers as it, and plain tools are stored, saved and shown to MCP byte for byte as before. A command that moves the running numbers away from a derived row stores it first. A waterjet (recipes) and an electrode (rpm 0) get none, so a sane tool never turns insane.
- **Stepdown and stepover per row** (mm, optional). They seed an operation's stepdown/stepover only inside an undoable command (quick-add, MCP `add_operation`, the feature recognizer, `SetWorkMaterial`, `SetStockMaterial`, retargeting a tool), never on load. Seeded kinds: pocket, adaptive, offset, slot, 3-D pocket, multi-axis rough, face (stepover; stepdown only when staged), 2-D contour (stepdown). A stepover wider than the cutter is refused by tool name.
- **Setup stock material.** New `StockMaterial` component on a setup's stock and the undoable `SetStockMaterial` command (MCP `set_stock_material`, stock page "Material" group). The row is picked by the stock's material, then the document's, then `Unknown`. The tools' running rpm/feed (the posted S word) follow the document material only - a tool is shared by every setup.
- **`.camtools`/project migration.** `PROJECT_VERSION` 62 -> 63 (the issue's "61 to 62" predates #1453's bump). A v62 project loads with each tool's own rpm/feed as its `Unknown` row; nothing it runs moves. `.camtools` reader accepts versions 1, 2 and 3; the writer writes 3 only when a library holds a stated `Unknown` row or a step (otherwise 1, or 2 for left-hand taps, as before). An `Unknown` row that only repeats the tool's own rpm/feed is not written, so plain tools save byte for byte as before (MCP `get_job` output unchanged for them).
- **Tool page.** The "Cutting data by material" group is now a table: Material, Spindle rpm, Feed, Stepdown, Stepover (0 = not stated). The `Unknown` row is first, its material fixed, not removable.
- **Behaviour change, inside a command only:** stating a document material the tool has no row for now runs the tool's `Unknown` row (before: the previous material's numbers stayed). An operation's milling feed still moves only for a row that names the material (#890's rule), so picking a material never overwrites hand-set op feeds.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2015-unknown-cutting-row.md` (why `Option<WorkMaterial>` and not a `WorkMaterial::Unknown` variant: `WorkMaterial::row()` indexes the handbook table).

Base: upstream/main (`31f8d03d7`); no file overlap with #2029 (it does not touch `tool_cutting_rows.rs`; both touch `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in different places). Fork synced at the current upstream main for this branch.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/tools/tests/unknown_row.rs` (6): selection order, step fallback, derivation once and only from the running numbers, kinds that get none, refusals (bad steps, `Unknown` twice).
- `crates/app/tests/cutting_unknown_row.rs` (9): `a_new_tool_gets_its_unknown_row_from_its_own_numbers`, `a_v62_project_loads_its_tool_numbers_as_the_unknown_row_with_no_loss`, `a_v1_tool_library_loads_with_the_unknown_row_and_steps_write_v3`, `the_row_is_picked_by_the_stock_then_the_document_then_unknown`, `a_second_setup_stock_material_seeds_only_its_own_operations`, `steps_seed_only_in_commands_and_the_stock_material_round_trips`, `a_project_with_no_new_rows_posts_the_same_s_and_f_words` (posts, re-saves as v62, reloads, re-posts: identical S/F words), `a_stated_stepover_wider_than_the_cutter_is_refused_by_tool_name`, `mcp_sets_the_stock_material_as_one_undo_step`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_material.rs`: the stock page's Material group sits between Shape and Size, and a pick is one undoable `SetStockMaterial`.
- Updated to the new law: `crates/app/tests/tool_cutting_rows.rs` (stating plastics, which has no row, now runs the tool's Unknown row), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutting_rows.rs` unit tests (Unknown is shown, never added).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (macOS, m5): green on 75031d5f9 (tools, app and ui suites; 6.2 min). Clippy on camcraft-tools, camcraft-app, camcraft-ui: clean (`--all-targets -D warnings`).

## UI before and after

These are headless captures of the real egui controls, rendered with `egui_kittest::Harness::render` on Linux. Before is pre-feature commit `31f8d03d744e77ce707282d816e11efe0922f239`. After is reviewed head `af78aec60436e402c8e026d5bc9521552131bf5a`. The temporary harness called the shipping `cutting_rows` and `stock_page` functions; no UI was mocked. The cutting-data draft has the same Aluminium 6061 row in both captures. The after draft also states stepdown 2 mm and stepover 3 mm. The stock captures use the same seeded document.

Images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, at commit `b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d`. No capture harness, screenshot, golden, or review evidence was added to this PR branch.

| Control | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cutting data | ![Cutting data before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/cutting-data-before.png) | ![Cutting data after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/cutting-data-after.png) |
| Stock Material | ![Stock Material before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/stock-material-before.png) | ![Stock Material after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b8e36213fceb86370d85ace7865d5ac48ddf1c4d/pr-2077/stock-material-after.png) |

The after table shows the fixed Unknown row, the named material row, and the step fields. The after stock page shows the Material group between Shape and Size. Both render checks passed at each revision (four captures total). This was a headless UI render, not a manual native-window session.

## Not exercised

- No manual native-window UI session. The controls were rendered headlessly as shown above. The release-lane pixel snapshot comparisons were not run and no golden PNG changed.
- The camcraft-mcp skill row for `set_stock_material` is a follow-up (process-file change): #2076.
- A per-setup spindle speed (the S word by stock material) is out of scope: the tool's running rpm follows the document material.

Changelog: Tools keep cutting data per work material with an Unknown default row, an optional stepdown and stepover per row, and a setup stock may state its own material, which picks the row (stock, then document, then Unknown); older projects and tool libraries load unchanged (#2015)

Effort: high (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: project files are written as version 63 (and tool libraries with a stated Unknown row or steps as version 3); older builds refuse them.

Fixes #2015

title: fix(post): honor or refuse G83 dwell per control
body:
Stacked on #1821 (merge #1821 first)

## What changed

Fanuc, Doosan DNM and Mazak refuse a positive G83 dwell by name.
Zero-dwell G83 remains available.
Haas keeps integer milliseconds and includes dwell in its G83 cycle signature.
Haas writes P0 to clear a previous dwell.

## Cause

The posts wrote P without checking G83 support for each control.
Haas omitted dwell from its cycle signature and omitted zero P.
That could reuse an earlier dwell.
Fanuc's standard milling G83 format has no P.
Mazak's detailed format and summary disagree, so this post refuses dwell conservatively.
The decision record links the public control manuals and explains these limits.

## Tests

Seven pins pass in camcraft-post's g83_dwell suite:

- fanuc_refuses_g83_dwell
- mazak_refuses_g83_dwell
- doosan_refuses_g83_dwell
- g83_without_dwell_remains_available
- haas_g83_writes_integer_milliseconds
- haas_g83_updates_dwell_in_an_open_cycle_group
- haas_g83_zero_dwell_clears_modal_p

Six pins failed on unchanged posts.
The existing Haas milliseconds behavior passed before the fix.
Replacing each of the four posts with upstream/main code made its affected pins fail.
Restoring each fix made them pass.
Removing the Haas signature change and the P0 change separately also failed their pins.
Restoring each change passed.

cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main passed with zero failures.
The final run took 18.2 minutes and included the expanded app integration selection.
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed separately for camcraft-post and camcraft-app.
The initial gate hit a sandbox denial in the optional sccache preprocessor directory.
Command-line Cargo configuration disabled that cache and cleared RUSTC_WRAPPER for the successful gate.
Repository configuration did not change.

## Goldens moved

crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_haas.nc adds P0 to its single G83 line.
No other golden change belongs to this issue.
The two-dot comparison against current upstream lists 139 golden files because the parent is older.
Each was checked against base-1821.
The inherited differences comprise decimal formatting, G76 fixtures, and the six parent bore fixtures.
Only the synth_haas P0 word differs from the parent in this patch.

## Not exercised

No real CNC control or GUI was exercised.
Doosan OEM MV0009OPE241_v0 behavior was not publicly verified.
Mazak G83 dwell support remains ambiguous in the cited manual.
Optional Fanuc small-hole mode is not selected by these posts.
Batch and release gates were not run.

## Overlaps

PR #1821 changes onCycle in the same four posts.
This branch starts at its head, 1c06a3e1.
PR #1738 touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
Its overlaps are formatting, block, toolNote, onParameter, afterOp and onProbeResult.
Neither the new test nor the changed golden overlaps an open PR.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Changelog: Refuse unsupported G83 dwell on Fanuc, Doosan and Mazak, and preserve or clear Haas G83 dwell correctly.

Fixes #1820

title: fix(2d): clear Zigzag rest boundaries without wall cusps
body:
Stacked on #1817 (merge #1817 first)

## What changed

2D rest machining now accepts Zigzag. It cuts rows, then closes each rest boundary to clear wall cusps.

Rows use an inset of `min(0.01 mm, stepover / 4)`. This prevents numeric boundary crossings without removing interior rows from small pockets.

The existing plain-pocket row algorithm moves unchanged to `pocket_zigzag.rs`. `pocket.rs` stays at 398 lines. No dependency is added.

The MCP skill now describes Zigzag support. Adaptive still has its named refusal. The entered previous tool remains an explicit trust assumption.

The remaining #1490 work has separate issues: Adaptive #2031, entry from cleared space #2032, and previous-operation stock #2033.

## Cause

Rows alone leave cusps at the rest boundary. A closing pass clears them. Rows that touch the boundary can cross it through numeric rounding.

A fixed 0.01 mm inset removes all rows from a tiny pocket. The stepover cap preserves those rows.

The geometry follows this project's existing scan and offset routines. See Held's [Zigzag Pocket Machining](https://www.cosy.sbg.ac.at/~held/projects/pocket_zig/pocket.html) and [pocket geometry monograph](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-54103-9). [Yao, Gupta and Nau](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~nau/papers/yao2003algorithms.pdf) provide the cutter-coverage context. The inset and closing-pass choices are ours.

## Tests

- `zigzag_rest_covers_corner_residue_without_gouges_or_unsafe_rapids`: red at the original refusal. Green after the fix. Covers both directions and 1.5/4 mm steps.
- `tiny_rest_pocket_keeps_interior_rows_when_previous_tool_fits_nowhere`: red with the fixed inset. Green with the stepover cap.
- Expected-change tests now accept Zigzag at the motion and operation parameter doors.
- Closing-pass mutation: red coverage; restored green. The first fixture left 287 measured residue points uncut.
- Zero-inset mutation: red verifier, with six crossings; restored green.
- Fixed-inset mutation: red tiny-pocket center coverage; restored green.
- Old `upstream/main` pocket code: red; restored green.
- Old `base-1817` rest strategy: red refusal; restored green. The parent baseline supplies the export absent from `upstream/main`.

The requested `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all three steps in 34.4 minutes before the inset cap.

After the cap, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only motion` passed its affected motion step in 663 seconds.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final code.

## Goldens moved

None from #1490. The diff against `base-1817` changes no `.nc` or `.cl` file.

The two-dot diff against `upstream/main` lists 147 files. All were checked against the merge base and parent.
Of these, 146 exactly reverse upstream changes absent from the older parent branch. The other is #1817's unchanged `pocket_rest_corners.cl` addition.

## Not exercised

No real machine was used. This change does not implement new Adaptive paths, cleared-space entry, or previous-operation stock input.
Those features require separate depth and cutter-clearance proofs in #2031, #2032, and #2033.

## Overlaps

- #1817 changes `rest_pocket`, `rest_strategy`, and the expected-refusal tests. This branch stacks on its head.
- #2013 and #1954 touch the same file, different module declarations in `machining2d/mod.rs`; whichever merges second refreshes.
- #1738 touches the same file, a different section of the MCP skill; whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1490-rest-strategies.md`.

Changelog: 2D rest Zigzag clears wall cusps with closing passes and preserves interior rows in small pockets.

Process change: yes

Effort: max

Fixes #1490

## UI images

title: fix(fidelity): a stock copy of an incomplete model keeps naming its hole
body:
A stock copied from an incomplete model (#1610) now keeps naming that model's hole after the model is deleted. Before this change, its refusal at the post fell back to "saved before CamCraft recorded mesh fidelity (project v58 or older)". The post still refused it; only the reason given was wrong.

Fixes #1700

## What changed

The copy's refusal read the hole from the source model by name (`mesh_open::unknown_note`), so once the source was gone the lookup found nothing. Now the copy carries the hole itself (`schema::MeshOpen`), beside the fidelity-unknown sentinel it already carried (#1056):

- **Where the hole is copied:** every place that lands the sentinel on a copy now lands the hole with it:
  - `SetStock` and its undo
  - a setup clone (`CreateSetup` with a datum)
  - an undone `DeleteSetup`
  - `UpdateModel`'s refresh of the copies, and its undo
  - the project loader
- **Where the refusal reads it:** `model_fidelity::op_problem` reads the hole off the entity that carries the sentinel. Two small helpers: `mesh_open::hole_behind` (the twin of `model_fidelity::chord_behind`) and `mesh_open::note_for`.
- **Project file:** the saver already wrote `mesh_open` for any entity that has one. The loader now also accepts it on a `FromModel` stock marked `fidelity_unknown`, and a hole without the mark stays corrupt. There is no version bump: #1610's check (a hole on anything but a model is corrupt) has not shipped in a cut yet, so no released reader refuses these files.

The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/1700-stock-copy-hole.md`.

## How tested

- **New:** `crates/app/tests/stock_copy_hole.rs` (6 tests). A copy carries the hole, and its refusal names the source and the hole:
  - after the source is deleted, and across undo and redo of that delete;
  - after save, load, and a second save that matches byte for byte;
  - through a setup clone and an undone setup delete;
  - through a whole re-import of the source (which clears it) and that re-import's undo;
  - through `SetStock`'s undo.

  The file also checks that a stock with a hole and no mark fails to load as corrupt.
- **Without the fix,** the two "source deleted" tests fail: the refusal reads "saved before CamCraft recorded …".
- **Existing tests:** the `import_step_open_shell` tests from #1610 still pass. Its corrupt-file message check passes too, because the new message keeps the old wording as a prefix.
- **Gate:** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (112 app suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branched from upstream/main after #1699 merged, not from a cut tag: the code this fixes is not in v0.20.0.

title: fix(ci): let the running post-merge gate finish
body:
## What changed

The running post-merge gate finishes when more merges arrive.
Set `cancel-in-progress: false` and update the queue comment.
Keep the existing concurrency group.

Needs maintainer: changes .github/workflows/post-merge.yml (one line).

## Cause

Each new merge cancelled the running gate.
A merge batch could leave only its last commit with a complete result.

## Tests

- `post_merge_preserves_running_gate` failed before the fix and passed after the fix.
- Mutation: restore the workflow from upstream/main. The pin failed. Restore the fix. The pin passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Goldens moved

None. The diff contains no changed `.nc` or `.cl` files.

## Not exercised

An actual merge batch must confirm the Actions queue behaviour after merge.
This draft does not start a workflow run.

## Overlaps

PR #1738 touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
It changes the runner labels in the gate and report jobs.
This PR changes the top-level concurrency setting and its comment.

Process change: yes

Effort: low

Changelog: Let a running post-merge gate finish when later merges arrive.

title: feat(contour): a picked start point with tabs on closed 2D contours
body:
## What changed

This is slice 2 of issue 1473: item 3, a picked start point with tabs on a closed 2D Contour.

- `pick_ring` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_start.rs`) does not refuse tabs now. Control and wear compensation with a pick stay refused by name.
- The new function `Ring::tab_keeps_from_start` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring.rs`) lays the tab windows from the pick. The tabs keep their count, width and equal spacing. Tab `i` spans `[(i+1)s - width, (i+1)s]`, where `s` is the spacing. The last tab ends on the seam, so no keep window crosses the seam.
- `contour` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs`) uses the new layout only when the ring has tabs and a pick. Thus every level, the tabbed levels too, enters at the pick. The lead-in law of the picked start runs on the first window only.
- A ring without a pick keeps the automatic tab layout, move for move.
- The exit point with tabs stays refused by name.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1473-start-point-tabs.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `a_picked_start_with_tabs_enters_every_level_at_its_projection` (`crates/motion/tests/contour_start.rs`)
- `tabs_without_a_pick_keep_their_automatic_windows` (same file)
- `picked_start_tab_windows_begin_at_the_start_and_never_cross_the_seam` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/tests.rs`)
- `control_compensation_with_a_pick_is_refused_by_name` (renamed; the tabs part of the old test is removed)

`cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test contour_start`: 13 passed. `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green on the head of this PR.

title: fix(post): refuse a bore dwell where G86 has no dwell word; pin G86 per post (#1445)
body:
## What changed

This is slice 2 of #1445: the boring cycle (G86: feed in, spindle stop, rapid out). The `Bore` cycle kind was already on main. This slice pins it per post and closes two dwell gaps.

- `assets/posts/{fanuc,haas,mazak,doosan-dnm,sinumerik}.cps`: a bore with a dwell is refused by name. Before this change, these posts wrote `P<ms>` on G86. The published Fanuc and Haas G86 formats have no P word, so the control dropped the dwell without a message. A bore with no dwell posts as before.
- tormach and grblhal keep `G86 ... P<seconds>` (the LinuxCNC G86 takes P as a dwell in seconds).
- The expanding posts (heidenhain, tinyg, carvera) refuse a bore by name on main (no spindle stop before the rapid retract). The tests pin that refusal and the app writes no NC file. Rejected intermediate program text can still contain fallback moves.
- New door `OpParams::dwell_refusal` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/dwell.rs`): a drilling dwell is a time from 0 to 3600 s (`MAX_DWELL_S`). `CreateOperation` and `EditOperationParams` refuse other values by name. MCP `edit_operation` uses the same command, so it refuses them too. The project loader does not use this door, so an old project still opens.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1445-boring-g86.md`.

The default posted output does not change. No existing NC or CL golden changed.

## Sources

- NIST IR 6556 (The NIST RS274NGC Interpreter v3), G86.
- The LinuxCNC G-code reference (G86 with P in seconds).
- The public Fanuc 30i operator manual (B-63944EN) and the Haas mill programming workbook, for the G86 address words.

No vendor post file or CAM output was read.

## How tested

- `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (7 tests): the stream round trip, G86 and no other cycle on the canned posts, the by-name dwell refusal on the Fanuc family and Sinumerik, `P0.5` on tormach and grblhal, the by-name refusal of the expanding posts, the refusal on posts without drilling, and new goldens in `crates/post/tests/golden/bore/` (fanuc, haas, sinumerik, grblhal, tormach).
- `crates/app/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (4 tests): undo and redo of a bore with a dwell and its generated chain, the by-name refusal of an insane dwell at command creation and edit, the MCP `edit_operation` door, and `refused_expanded_bores_write_no_nc_file` for all three expanding posts with and without a dwell.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (154 steps, 0 failed). App/post all-target Clippy passes with `-D warnings`. Each review fix was mutation-checked: RED when removed, GREEN when restored.

## Not exercised

- No real control ran this output: Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Doosan, Sinumerik, Heidenhain, grblHAL, PathPilot, TinyG and Carvera.
- The grblHAL and Sinumerik ISO forms of G86 with P are not verified from a manual.
- The P dwell on the Fanuc-family G83 is not checked (follow-up below).
- The GUI was not launched. The batch tier was not run.

## Follow-ups

- #1819: the expanded bore on heidenhain, tinyg and carvera stops the spindle at the bottom.
- #1820: check that the Fanuc-family posts do not drop a dwell on G83.
- #1479 (fine boring G76), #1480 (G89), #1481 (ream on lathe posts) stay open from slice 1.

Changelog: The Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Doosan and Sinumerik posts refuse a bore (G86) with a dwell by name, because their G86 has no dwell word; a drilling dwell outside 0 to 3600 s is refused when the operation is made or edited (#1445)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #1445

The status strip gains a Report door next to the Debug info door (#1696).
It opens a small window:

- Two buttons, "Report a bug" and "Request a feature". Each opens the
  browser on a prefilled GitHub new-issue URL: the title, the body and the

- A "Copy screenshot" button. It puts a picture of the current document

fields from one source. An empty document refuses the copy in words, in the
status line.

The repository also gains `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/blank-issue.md` and
`.github/config.yml`. GitHub's prefill query works only on a blank
template, not on the issue forms. The new glyph `act-report.png` comes from
an original SVG master, `assets/ui/svg/act-report.svg`.

- `report_tests.rs` (new, kittest): URL encoding, the prefilled URL shape,
  the body content, the door open/close, the typed title in the URL, the

- `structural.rs`: the door sits on the status strip; no floating window is

title: feat(wcs): store WCS axis flips (Flip X/Y/Z); refuse post and generation by name
body:
Base: `main`. The parent PR #1717 merged. Head `ffc673589` has `origin/main` at `3f41b8da6` merged in.

## What changed

Part 1 of issue 1649 ("Split in two"): the WCS page can store a flipped axis. This PR does not change posted G-code.

- **Stored flags.** A new component `schema::WcsFlip([bool; 3])` is on the setup's WCS entity. "No flip" is stored as no component.
- **One undoable command.** `SetWcsFlip::for_setup` sets the flags of a setup's WCS. It refuses an unknown setup by name. If the WCS was never placed, it places it at the identity, and undo removes it again.
- **WCS page.** Three toggles, "Flip X", "Flip Y" and "Flip Z", are under the quarter turns. A lit toggle is a flipped axis. When an axis is flipped, a note tells the user that posting and generating are refused until the flip is cleared.
- **Viewport triad.** A flipped axis is drawn in the opposite direction. A flipped WCS at the origin does not hide the world axes.
- **Refusal by name.** The post verification gate (`verification_report_by`) and the generation door (`collect_job`) refuse a flipped WCS. An example message: "the WCS (G54) has its X axis flipped; posting or generating with a flipped WCS is not available yet - clear the flip on the WCS page (operations: Face1)". All post paths use the gate (`post_script_body_with`, `posting_mounts`, `posting_per_op`), so no path posts with a flip set. The WCS word comes from `setup::wcs_name`, the existing derivation.
- **Project file v67.** A WCS row can have the optional key `flip` (`{"x": true}`), and only flipped axes are written. A file without the key opens with no flip. A `flip` key on a row that is not a WCS is refused as corrupt. Main used v62 to v66 for other keys, so this PR takes v67.
- **Undo keeps the flip.** `DeleteEntity`, `DeleteSetup` and the datum transfer of `CreateSetup` keep the flip.
- **MCP.** A new tool, `set_wcs_flip {x?, y?, z?, setup?}`. An axis that is not given keeps its flag. `get_job` shows `setups[].wcs.flip`. The camcraft-mcp skill has the tool row and a "Shipped" line.
- **Decisions.** `docs/decisions/1720-wcs-flip-flags.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/wcs_flip.rs` (10 tests). It pins these points:
  - the command, undo and redo;
  - the refusal of an unknown setup;
  - the post refusal by name, and the same stream after the flip is cleared;
  - the generation refusal by name;
  - the setup name in the message;
  - DeleteSetup and DeleteEntity undo;
  - the datum transfer;
  - the project round trip, an old file, and a corrupt row;
  - the MCP tool and `get_job`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_flip_tests.rs` (3 tests). It pins the toggle layout and live state, the click to the command, the reversed triad, undo and redo, and the status line.

Gate on head `ffc673589` (debug, `-j 6`, `--test-threads=6`, narrow ladder):

- `camcraft-app`, 29 test binaries, all pass:
  - pinning and project version: `wcs_flip` 10, `program_info` 10, `project_roundtrip` 73, `trunnion_schema` 2, `tilt_basis_compat` 5, `break_through` 7, `tap_hand` 7, `units_migrate` 5.
  - WCS: `one_wcs` 8, `setup_wcs` 7, `setup_relative` 9, `wcs_tilt` 2, `wcs_index` 4, `wcs_align` 5, `wcs_roles` 9, `rotated_wcs` 9.
  - MCP: `mcp_setup` 9, `mcp_work_offset` 4, `mcp_wcs_features` 2, `mcp_verify` 3.
  - post gate: `post_not_judged` 4, `carried_verify` 8, `setup_mounts_post` 8, `setup_mount` 6, `rotary_verify` 9, `stock_source_verdict` 22, `index_swing` 13, `wire_verify` 3, `probe_only_sim` 2.
- `camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`): 1004 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` selects all app and ui suites (394 steps), because the PR touches `schema.rs` and `project/`. That run took more than 20 minutes before, so this refresh used the narrow ladder.

## Not exercised

- Posting with a flip (part 2 of issue 1649) is not in this PR. There are no NC golden changes.
- No script verb. The decision file gives the reason.
- The full app suite set (the quick gate selection) did not run on this head.
- The Flip toggles stay enabled on a mill. Main now disables the X and Y quarter turns on a mill (`MILL_TILT_HINT`). A flip is refused at post and generation, so no output changes.

Changelog: The WCS page can store a flipped X, Y or Z axis (Flip X / Flip Y / Flip Z, MCP `set_wcs_flip`); a setup with a flipped axis is refused by name at post and generation until part 2 carries the flip into the program; project files are now v67.

Effort: high

Process change: yes

## Screenshots

Before (the #1717 head): the quarter turns show Turn X/Y/Z buttons and no Flip row.

![before](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/98d3ca71cf377bb91b111367ce60380d2c84e30b/pr-1738/before.png?raw=true)

After (this PR): a Flip X, Flip Y and Flip Z row sits under the quarter turns.

title: fix(post): state the stock's turning radius on lathe streams
body:
Stacked on #1667 (the G30 logic of the Tormach lathe post). The diff shows the commits of #1667 until #1667 merges.

## What changed

- `Dump` in `camcraft-post` gets the field `stock_turn_radius`. When it is set, finite and more than 0, the stream gets `PARAM StockTurnRadius` after `StockZTop`.
- The new module `crates/app/src/stock_turn.rs` calculates the radius: the largest distance of a stock mesh vertex from the spindle axis (the world Z line through the setup origin).
- `posting.rs` sets the radius only for a lathe or mill-turn setup. Mill streams do not change.
- `tormach-lathe.cps`: `stockEnv()` uses the larger of the box half-width and `StockTurnRadius`. Thus the G30 approach and departure clear the rotating corners of a square bar.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` does not read the stock. It does not change.
- `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` gets a row for the new property.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/1666-stock-turn-radius.md`.

## Posted G-code changes

Yes, for a lathe program on a box (square bar) stock with the Tormach lathe post. The G30 departure goes to the corner diameter, not to the box width. A round bar gives the same radius as before, so its output does not change. No real control ran the output.

## Updated goldens

The two axial-drill goldens now contain the corner-clearance departure:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/axial_drill_mm.nc`: the last move changes from `G0 X24` to `G0 X33.941`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/axial_drill_inch.nc`: the last move changes from `G0 X0.9449` to `G0 X1.3363`.

The fixture uses a 24 x 24 box stock. Its corners turn on a circle of radius 16.971 mm (diameter 33.941 mm). The updated goldens match this clearance. `lathe_post_tormach::an_axial_drill_posts_as_plain_moves_in_mm_and_inch` passes.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_turn_radius.rs`:

- `a_lathe_stream_states_the_radius_its_stock_sweeps`
- `a_mill_stream_states_no_turning_radius`
- `the_g30_moves_use_the_square_bars_corner_circle`
- `a_square_bar_program_has_no_g30_rapid_inside_the_corners_circle`

All four pass. The author-side validation on head `156dec8d689f539bfdcc01b3b39727af8d85dd02` reported a passing `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 421 post tests and 3023 app tests passed, with 22 app tests ignored. It also reported passing `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

The latest review tested a local trial merge with upstream main `4e0b9abefcb225595d47d9c69a2482d6359b190f`. All 96 selected app and post tests passed. These included all eight `lathe_post_tormach` tests and all four `lathe_post_turn_radius` tests. The review also reported passing `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`. It ran the quick-gate plan with `--dry-run`, rather than the full gate.

The author-side fix and the latest review checked mutations of the stream parameter and `stockEnv()` radius use. The tests failed with each mutation and passed after restoration. The author-side fix also checked the G30 motion-block test and each axial-drill golden by reverting each fix. Each test failed after the revert and passed after restoration.

Not exercised: a real PathPilot control, mill-turn posts, and the UI.

Changelog: The Tormach lathe post now clears the corners of a square-bar stock in its G30 approach and departure moves (the stream states StockTurnRadius).

Effort: high (no escalation).

Fixes #1666

title: feat(ui): drag a part along an axis with move handles (#1198 b)
body:
#1198 slice (b): move handles with drag-to-move. Slice (a), the bottom bar, merged in #1203. Slice (c), the rotate handles, is #2047. Slice (d), snapping and typed values, stays on #1198.

**GUI hand check needed.** The kittest harness and headless state tests test the handles, the drag and the readout. The offscreen screenshots below come from the same harness. Nobody has examined them on a real screen with real mouse input.

## What changed
- **Move mode in the bottom bar.** A new bar button (a four-armed cross, after Pick through) turns `State::move_handles` on and off. It is off by default. It is view state like Pick through, and it queues no command.
- **Handles** (`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`, painted by `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`). With Move on and exactly one shown part selected, three arms in the axis colours start at the bounding-box centre of the part. Each arm ends in a ball. The arms stay 70 px long on screen at all zoom levels. The ball under the pointer is drawn larger.
- **Drag.** A press on a ball takes the press before orbit and pick. A press on empty space still orbits. When a nav tool of the bar (Orbit, Pan, Zoom) is latched, that tool owns the press. While the button is down, the preview moves the body along the axis (`world.rs` draws it with an offset) and never writes the world. The signed distance shows above the bar. The distance is the point where the cursor ray is nearest to the axis line, so the part stays under the cursor in perspective and in ortho.
- **One command per drag.** The release queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy { name, delta }`. The drain (`crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs`) runs it as the `MoveModel::new` of the Model page, with the rotation copied bit for bit. Thus a drag is one undo step, with the same staleness, the same following stock and the same fixture-clash warning as a typed move. There is no new placement path.
- **No history step for:** Escape during a drag (the key is consumed), a drag that ends at its start point, and Move turned off.
- **Turned setups.** When the active setup holds the part turned (#326), the drag occurs in the frame of that setup. The shown delta is rotated back into the document frame, so the part moves along the axis that the user sees.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/1198-drag-to-move.md`: only parts are dragged in this slice, Move mode is off by default, and the preview moves the body only.

## MCP
No new app command, thus no new MCP tool. `MoveModelBy` is a UI queue verb over the existing `MoveModel`. The MCP `move_model` tool (`crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs`) already places a part through `MoveModel`. An agent can make each move that a drag makes.

## Screenshots (offscreen, kittest harness with the headless GPU viewport)
The "before" is Move off on this branch: on `main` the bar has no Move button, and all else is the same.

| Move off (before) | Move on |
|---|---|
| ![Move off](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/screenshots/pr-1330/1-move-off.png?raw=true) | ![Move on](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/screenshots/pr-1330/2-move-on.png?raw=true) |

| X ball dragged (preview, readout above the bar) | After the release (one `MoveModel`) |
|---|---|
| ![Dragging](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/screenshots/pr-1330/3-dragging.png?raw=true) | ![Released](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/screenshots/pr-1330/4-released.png?raw=true) |

## Refresh for merge (2026-11-15)
- Old head: `e50da95c3`. New head: `58df4b729` (merge of `origin/main` at `17a8c6e76`). No rebase, no force-push.
- The merge had no conflicts. No file was edited by hand.
- `git diff origin/main --stat` lists only the 13 files of this PR.

## How tested (on the new head, debug, `-j 6`, `--test-threads=6`)
- camcraft-ui lib, filter `body_drag move_drag viewport_bar view_cube structural pick_through box_select`: 37 passed, 0 failed. This includes:
  - `egui_app::tests::body_drag` (kittest, the real shell; 5 tests): `handles_show_only_in_move_mode_on_a_selected_part`, `a_ball_drag_is_one_undoable_move_by_the_dragged_distance`, `escape_mid_drag_cancels_with_no_history_step`, `a_drag_that_ends_where_it_began_adds_nothing`, `empty_space_still_orbits_in_move_mode`.
  - `move_drag_tests` (headless state; 5 tests): `the_drag_distance_is_the_axis_point_under_the_cursor`, `a_press_off_the_balls_is_not_a_drag`, `a_turned_setup_moves_the_part_along_the_axis_it_shows`, `the_rotation_is_kept_bit_for_bit`, `a_non_finite_distance_is_refused_by_name`.
  - The bar laws with the new button: `viewport_bar::tests::bar_fits_its_buttons` and `law_tests::view_cube_tests::the_hud_is_laid_out_from_the_pane_alone` (it iterates each button in `NAVS`), the structural twin and the pick-through and box-select tests.
- camcraft-ui `--test shell`: 21 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- A real screen and real mouse input. GUI hand check needed.
- Pixel snapshots (release lane). The bar is wider, so the viewport goldens differ. They are made again at the cut. This PR changes no PNG.
- The other ui integration suites and the other crates. This PR changes only `camcraft-ui` and one decision file.
- Fixtures and the stock cannot be dragged (recorded decision).

## Open notes for the review
- The Move icon (four arms with balls) and the Pan icon (four arrows) look almost the same in the bar (see the screenshots). A reviewer must decide if one of them needs a different glyph.
- `shell.rs` (1043 lines) and `viewport_bar.rs` (461 lines) were already more than 400 lines on `main` (1028 and 433). This PR adds only its own lines to them.

Changelog: Viewport: a Move button in the bottom bar puts axis handles on the selected part; dragging a ball moves the part along that axis, one undo step per drag (#1198 b)
